dravatāṃ samanuprāptāṃ tāṃ vijñāya niśākaraḥ .. 47 ..
1.106.d:
तस्याः स्पर्शोपलम्भेन द्रवीभूतः स दानवः ॥
द्रवतां समनुप्राप्तां तां विज्ञाय निशाकरः ॥ 47 ॥
1.106.m: Upon experiencing her touch, that Dānava liquefied. / Knowing that she had attained liquidity, the night-maker,

1.106.s:
mamantha sahasā toyaṃ putrārthī manujeśvara ..
mathyamāne jale tena tadā somena pārthiva .. 48 ..
1.106.d:
ममन्थ सहसा तोयं पुत्रार्थी मनुजेश्वर ॥
मथ्यमाने जले तेन तदा सोमेन पार्थिव ॥ 48 ॥
1.106.m: desiring a son, suddenly churned the water, O ruler of men. / As the water was being churned by Soma at that time, O king,

1.106.s:
viveśa tejasi payo viṣṇurdevanamaskṛtaḥ ..
tataḥ kumārassañjāto budhastu grahabodhanaḥ ..49..
1.106.d:
विवेश तेजसि पयो विष्णुर्देवनमस्कृतः ॥
ततः कुमारस्सञ्जातो बुधस्तु ग्रहबोधनः ॥49॥
1.106.m: Viṣṇu, who is revered by the gods, entered the water with his splendour. / Then a youth was born: Mercury, who awakens the planets.

1.106.s:
taddadhāra tadā tārā gurupatnī yaśasvinī..
yadā dhārayituṃ śaktā na bālaṃ tejasānvitam..1.106.50..
1.106.d:
तद्दधार तदा तारा गुरुपत्नी यशस्विनी॥
यदा धारयितुं शक्ता न बालं तेजसान्वितम्॥1.106.50॥
1.106.m: Then Tārā, the renowned wife of the Guru, received him. / When she was unable to bear the child endowed with fiery energy,

1.106.s:
dākṣāyaṇī cotsasarja candrapatnī sutaṃ tadā ..
evaṃ janma budhasyoktaṃ jīvasyātaḥ paraṃ śṛṇu ..51..
1.106.d:
दाक्षायणी चोत्ससर्ज चन्द्रपत्नी सुतं तदा ॥
एवं जन्म बुधस्योक्तं जीवस्यातः परं शृणु ॥51॥
1.106.m: the daughter of Dakṣa, the wife of the Moon, then released the son. / Thus the birth of Mercury has been told; hereafter hear that of Jupiter.

1.106.s:
surūpā nāma duhitā mārīcestu prajāpateḥ ..
dattā tvaṅgirase sā tu rūpayauvanaśālinī..52..
1.106.d:
सुरूपा नाम दुहिता मारीचेस्तु प्रजापतेः ॥
दत्ता त्वङ्गिरसे सा तु रूपयौवनशालिनी॥52॥
1.106.m: A daughter of the Prajāpati Marīci named Surūpā, / endowed with beauty and youth, was given to Aṅgiras.

1.106.s:
tasyāṃ sa janayāmāsa devācāryaṃ bṛhaspatim ..
bṛhadvācaṃ mahābuddhiṃ vedavedāṅgapāragam .. 93 ..
1.106.d:
तस्यां स जनयामास देवाचार्यं बृहस्पतिम् ॥
बृहद्वाचं महाबुद्धिं वेदवेदाङ्गपारगम् ॥ 93 ॥
1.106.m: Upon her he begot Bṛhaspati, the teacher of the gods, / of lofty speech, of great intellect, who has mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

1.106.s:
uktaṃ te janma jīvasya śukrasyātaḥ paraṃ śṛṇu .
uṣā nāma tathā kanyā hiraṇyakaśipossutā .. 54 ..
1.106.d:
उक्तं ते जन्म जीवस्य शुक्रस्यातः परं शृणु ।
उषा नाम तथा कन्या हिरण्यकशिपोस्सुता ॥ 54 ॥
1.106.m: The birth of Jupiter has been told to you; hereafter hear that of Venus. / There was a maiden named Uṣā, the daughter of Hiraṇyakaśipu,

1.106.s:
bhṛgupatnī viśālākṣī sarvalokaikasundarī ..
janayāmāsa dharmajñaṃ khyātamauśanasaṃ prabhum .. 55 ..
1.106.d:
भृगुपत्नी विशालाक्षी सर्वलोकैकसुन्दरी ॥
जनयामास धर्मज्ञं ख्यातमौशनसं प्रभुम् ॥ 55 ॥
1.106.m: the large-eyed wife of Bhṛgu, the sole beauty of all the worlds; / she gave birth to the lord known as Auśanasa, who knows dharma.

1.106.s:
sa jahārātha yogātmā dhanaṃ vaiśravaṇasya tu ..
hṛte vitte tu yakṣeśo jagāma śaraṇaṃ haram .. 56 ..
1.106.d:
स जहाराथ योगात्मा धनं वैश्रवणस्य तु ॥
हृते वित्ते तु यक्षेशो जगाम शरणं हरम् ॥ 56 ॥
1.106.m: He, possessing yogic power, stole the wealth of Vaiśravaṇa. / When his wealth was stolen, the lord of the yakṣas sought refuge with Hara.

1.106.s:
tataḥ kruddho mahādevo bhārgavaṃ hantumudyataḥ ..
bhārgavo'pi ca yogena praviveśa haraṃ tadā .. 57 ..
1.106.d:
ततः क्रुद्धो महादेवो भार्गवं हन्तुमुद्यतः ॥
भार्गवोऽपि च योगेन प्रविवेश हरं तदा ॥ 57 ॥
1.106.m: Then Mahādeva, enraged, prepared to slay the Bhārgava; / but the Bhārgava, by yoga, entered Hara at that time.

1.106.s:
harodarasthastuṣṭāva devīṃ parvatanandinīm ..
tayoktastaṃ tu tatyāja tadā śiśnena śaṅkaraḥ .. 58 ..
1.106.d:
हरोदरस्थस्तुष्टाव देवीं पर्वतनन्दिनीम् ॥
तयोक्तस्तं तु तत्याज तदा शिश्नेन शङ्करः ॥ 58 ॥
1.106.m: Standing within the belly of Hara, he praised the goddess, the daughter of the mountain; / spoken to by her, Śaṅkara then discharged him through his phallus.

1.106.s:
śukrastu nāma caivāsya tadā cakre jagadguruḥ ..
dhaneśatvaṃ dadau cāsya dhaneśena sahānagha .. 59 ..
1.106.d:
शुक्रस्तु नाम चैवास्य तदा चक्रे जगद्गुरुः ॥
धनेशत्वं ददौ चास्य धनेशेन सहानघ ॥ 59 ॥
1.106.m: Then the teacher of the world gave him the name Śukra (semen). / And he granted him lordship over wealth together with the lord of wealth, O sinless one,

1.106.s:
maitryaṃ cāsya dhaneśena tathā cakre trilocanaḥ ..
śanaiścarasya vakṣyāmi janmātaste nareśvara .. 1.106.60 ..
1.106.d:
मैत्र्यं चास्य धनेशेन तथा चक्रे त्रिलोचनः ॥
शनैश्चरस्य वक्ष्यामि जन्मातस्ते नरेश्वर ॥ 1.106.60 ॥
1.106.m: and the three-eyed god established friendship for him with the lord of wealth. / Hereafter I shall relate to you the birth of Saturn, O ruler of men.

1.106.s:
brahmaṇo mānasaḥ putrastvaṣṭā nāma prajāpatiḥ ..
saṃjñāṃ tu janayāmāsa kanyāṃ trailokyasundarīm .. 61 ..
1.106.d:
ब्रह्मणो मानसः पुत्रस्त्वष्टा नाम प्रजापतिः ॥
संज्ञां तु जनयामास कन्यां त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरीम् ॥ 61 ॥
1.106.m: The mind-born son of Brahmā, the Prajāpati named Tvaṣṭṛ, / begot a daughter named Saṃjñā, the beauty of the three worlds.

1.106.s:
tāṃ dadau savituḥ patnīṃ tasyāṃ sūryo mahātapāḥ ..
janayāmāsa dharmajñaṃ manuṃ vaivasvataṃ prabhuma .. 62..
1.106.d:
तां ददौ सवितुः पत्नीं तस्यां सूर्यो महातपाः ॥
जनयामास धर्मज्ञं मनुं वैवस्वतं प्रभुम ॥ 62॥
1.106.m: He gave her as a wife to Savitṛ; upon her the Sun, of great asceticism, / begot the lord Vaivasvata Manu, who knows dharma,

1.106.s:
yamaṃ ca yamunāṃ caiva trailokyasyaikapālinīma ..
teṣu jñāteṣu putreṣu saṃjñā sā cārulocanā .. 63 ..
1.106.d:
यमं च यमुनां चैव त्रैलोक्यस्यैकपालिनीम ॥
तेषु ज्ञातेषु पुत्रेषु संज्ञा सा चारुलोचना ॥ 63 ॥
1.106.m: and Yama, and Yamunā, the sole protector of the three worlds. / When those children were known, she, Saṃjñā of charming eyes,

1.106.s:
bhartustejo'tidurdharṣamasahantī varāṅganā ..
sā tu cchāyāṃ samāhūya idaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 64 ..
1.106.d:
भर्तुस्तेजोऽतिदुर्धर्षमसहन्ती वराङ्गना ॥
सा तु च्छायां समाहूय इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 64 ॥
1.106.m: that excellent woman, unable to endure the exceedingly irresistible splendour of her husband, / summoned Chāyā and spoke these words:

1.106.s:
madrūpeṇa tvayā bhadre vastavyamavikārayā ..
pālanīyau ca me putrau tvayemau duhitā ca me .. 65 ..
1.106.d:
मद्रूपेण त्वया भद्रे वस्तव्यमविकारया ॥
पालनीयौ च मे पुत्रौ त्वयेमौ दुहिता च मे ॥ 65 ॥
1.106.m: "In my form, good woman, you must remain without alteration, / and you must protect these two sons of mine and my daughter."

1.106.s:
evamuktā yayau devī pitaraṃ varavarṇinī ..
pitrā nirastā bhartāraṃ gacchagaccheti bhāṣitā .. 66 ..
1.106.d:
एवमुक्ता ययौ देवी पितरं वरवर्णिनी ॥
पित्रा निरस्ता भर्तारं गच्छगच्छेति भाषिता ॥ 66 ॥
1.106.m: Having spoken thus, the goddess of fair complexion went to her father. / Rejected by her father, who told her, "Go, go to your husband,"

1.106.s:
uttarāṃstu kurūngatvā vaḍavārūpadhāriṇī ..
cacāra śādvalāñchubhrānvaneṣūpavaneṣu ca .. 67 ..
1.106.d:
उत्तरांस्तु कुरून्गत्वा वडवारूपधारिणी ॥
चचार शाद्वलाञ्छुभ्रान्वनेषूपवनेषु च ॥ 67 ॥
1.106.m: she went to the Northern Kurus, took the form of a mare, / and wandered the bright green pastures in the forests and groves.

1.106.s:
chāyāyāṃ ca tathārkopi saṃjñeyamiti cintayan ..
dvau putrau janayāmāsa sāvarṇaṃ tu śanaiścaram .. 68 ..
1.106.d:
छायायां च तथार्कोपि संज्ञेयमिति चिन्तयन् ॥
द्वौ पुत्रौ जनयामास सावर्णं तु शनैश्चरम् ॥ 68 ॥
1.106.m: And the sun also, thinking, "This is Saṃjñā," on Chāyā / fathered two sons, Sāvarṇa and Śanaiścara.

1.106.s:
vajra uvāca ..
kathaṃ tāmāptavānsaṃjñāṃ bhūya eva divākaraḥ ..
etanme saṃśayaṃ brūhi bhṛguvaṃśavivardhana .. 69 ..
1.106.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
कथं तामाप्तवान्संज्ञां भूय एव दिवाकरः ॥
एतन्मे संशयं ब्रूहि भृगुवंशविवर्धन ॥ 69 ॥
1.106.m: Vajra said: / How did the sun obtain Saṃjñā once again? / Tell me this, [clearing] my doubt, O enlarger of the line of Bhṛgu.

1.106.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
putrayoḥ sūtaputrām̐stu yathā chāyānuvartate ..
na tathā vartate devī saṃjñāsūteṣu bhāminī .. 1.106.70 ..
1.106.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
पुत्रयोः सूतपुत्राम्̐स्तु यथा छायानुवर्तते ॥
न तथा वर्तते देवी संज्ञासूतेषु भामिनी ॥ 1.106.70 ॥
1.106.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / As Chāyā treated the sons she herself had borne, / the passionate lady did not treat the sons borne of Saṃjñā.

1.106.s:
tataḥ kadācittāṃ kruddhaḥ saṃtatarja tadā yamaḥ ..
taṃ śaśāpa tadā cchāyā pādaste patatāmayam .. 71 ..
1.106.d:
ततः कदाचित्तां क्रुद्धः संततर्ज तदा यमः ॥
तं शशाप तदा च्छाया पादस्ते पततामयम् ॥ 71 ॥
1.106.m: Then once Yama, angered, threatened her, / and Chāyā cursed him: "Let this foot of yours fall off!"

1.106.s:
yamaḥ śaśaṃsa tatsarvaṃ pituḥ parabalārdanaḥ ..
śrutvā yamasya vacanaṃ yamaṃ provāca bhāskaraḥ .. 72 ..
1.106.d:
यमः शशंस तत्सर्वं पितुः परबलार्दनः ॥
श्रुत्वा यमस्य वचनं यमं प्रोवाच भास्करः ॥ 72 ॥
1.106.m: Yama, the crusher of the enemy host, related all of that to his father. / Having heard Yama's word, the sun said to Yama:

1.106.s:
kṛmayo māṃsamādāya tathā yāsyanti bhūtalam ..
evaṃ śāmyecca śāpaste tvaṃ ca trāto bhaviṣyasi .. 73 ...
1.106.d:
कृमयो मांसमादाय तथा यास्यन्ति भूतलम् ॥
एवं शाम्येच्च शापस्ते त्वं च त्रातो भविष्यसि ॥ 73 ॥।
1.106.m: "Worms will take the flesh and carry it to the surface of the earth; / thus your curse will be appeased, and you will be saved."

1.106.s:
etacchrutvā piturvākyaṃ cakāra sumahattapaḥ ..
ārādhayāmāsa tadā devadevaṃ janārdanam .. 74 ..
1.106.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा पितुर्वाक्यं चकार सुमहत्तपः ॥
आराधयामास तदा देवदेवं जनार्दनम् ॥ 74 ॥
1.106.m: Having heard this speech of his father, he performed very great austerity, / and he then propitiated Janārdana, the god of gods.

1.106.s:
tasmātsa lebhe dharmātmā dharmarājatvamañjasā ..
sūryo'pyavindam̐stattvena putraśāpasya kāraṇam ..75..
1.106.d:
तस्मात्स लेभे धर्मात्मा धर्मराजत्वमञ्जसा ॥
सूर्योऽप्यविन्दम्̐स्तत्त्वेन पुत्रशापस्य कारणम् ॥75॥
1.106.m: From him that righteous-minded one quickly obtained the kingship of dharma; / and the sun also discovered the true cause of his son's curse.

1.106.s:
krodhāviṣṭastadā chāyāṃ papracchāmitraghātanaḥ..
śaśaṃsa tasya sā sarvaṃ yathāvṛttamaninditā ..76..
1.106.d:
क्रोधाविष्टस्तदा छायां पप्रच्छामित्रघातनः॥
शशंस तस्य सा सर्वं यथावृत्तमनिन्दिता ॥76॥
1.106.m: Filled with anger, the slayer of foes then questioned Chāyā; / and she, blameless, related to him everything just as it happened.

1.106.s:
śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasyāstvaṣṭurveśmāgamadraviḥ ..
na dadarśa ca tatrasthāṃ tāṃ bhāryāṃ śubhacāriṇīm .. 77 ..
1.106.d:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्यास्त्वष्टुर्वेश्मागमद्रविः ॥
न ददर्श च तत्रस्थां तां भार्यां शुभचारिणीम् ॥ 77 ॥
1.106.m: Hearing her word, the sun went to the dwelling of Tvaṣṭṛ, / and he did not see there his wife of auspicious conduct.

1.106.s:
tvaṣṭrā cāśaṃsitaṃ tasya vaḍavārūpadhāriṇī..
asahantī tu tejaste kurūnāvasate śubhā .. 78 ..
1.106.d:
त्वष्ट्रा चाशंसितं तस्य वडवारूपधारिणी॥
असहन्ती तु तेजस्ते कुरूनावसते शुभा ॥ 78 ॥
1.106.m: And it was declared to him by Tvaṣṭṛ: "Assuming the form of a mare, / unable to endure your splendour, the auspicious woman dwells in the Kurus."

1.106.s:
bhramimāveśya deveśaṃ tvaṣṭāpi jagatāṃ patim ..
tejasaḥ śātanaṃ cakre devasya savitustadā..79 ..
1.106.d:
भ्रमिमावेश्य देवेशं त्वष्टापि जगतां पतिम् ॥
तेजसः शातनं चक्रे देवस्य सवितुस्तदा॥79 ॥
1.106.m: Then Tvaṣṭṛ mounted the lord of the gods, the master of the worlds, upon the lathe / and performed the paring down of the splendour of the god Savitṛ.

1.106.s:
kīrṇe tejasi tadrūpaṃ bhṛśaṃ kāntataraṃ sthitam ..
śīrṇena tejasā cakraṃ tvaṣṭā cakre jagadguroḥ .. 1.106.80 ..
1.106.d:
कीर्णे तेजसि तद्रूपं भृशं कान्ततरं स्थितम् ॥
शीर्णेन तेजसा चक्रं त्वष्टा चक्रे जगद्गुरोः ॥ 1.106.80 ॥
1.106.m: When the splendour had been scattered, his form became exceedingly radiant. / Out of that cut-off splendour, Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the discus of the guru of the world,

1.106.s:
sudarśanamiti khyātaṃ devasya harimedhasaḥ ..
kāntarūpastu savitā hayarūpadharastadā .. 81 ..
1.106.d:
सुदर्शनमिति ख्यातं देवस्य हरिमेधसः ॥
कान्तरूपस्तु सविता हयरूपधरस्तदा ॥ 81 ॥
1.106.m: known as Sudarśana, belonging to the god of golden splendour. / Then Savitṛ, having a radiant form, assumed the form of a horse

1.106.s:
uttarāṃstu kurūngatvā vaḍavārūpadhāriṇīm ..
svāṃ dadarśa tadā bhāryāṃ śītaladravyasaṃyutām ..82 ..
1.106.d:
उत्तरांस्तु कुरून्गत्वा वडवारूपधारिणीम् ॥
स्वां ददर्श तदा भार्यां शीतलद्रव्यसंयुताम् ॥82 ॥
1.106.m: and, going to the Northern Kurus, beheld his wife / who had taken the form of a mare and was endowed with cool qualities.

1.106.s:
maithunārthī tu tāṃ devo jagāma tvaritastadā ..
vegavantaṃ tu samprāptaṃ dṛṣṭvā turagamuttamam .. 83 ..
1.106.d:
मैथुनार्थी तु तां देवो जगाम त्वरितस्तदा ॥
वेगवन्तं तु सम्प्राप्तं दृष्ट्वा तुरगमुत्तमम् ॥ 83 ॥
1.106.m: Desiring union, the god approached her swiftly. / But seeing the excellent horse arrived with great speed,

1.106.s:
vyaceṣṭata ca sā devī parapuṃsopaśaṅkayā ..
mukhe ca bhāvayāmāsa tāṃ sūryo dīptadīdhitiḥ .. 84 ..
1.106.d:
व्यचेष्टत च सा देवी परपुंसोपशङ्कया ॥
मुखे च भावयामास तां सूर्यो दीप्तदीधितिः ॥ 84 ॥
1.106.m: the goddess struggled, fearing he was another male. / And the sun of blazing rays discharged [his seed] into her mouth.

1.106.s:
tasyā nāsāpuṭau pūrṇau tadā śukreṇa pārthiva ..
tathā tasyāstadā jātau nāsatyāvaśvināvubhau .. 85 ..
1.106.d:
तस्या नासापुटौ पूर्णौ तदा शुक्रेण पार्थिव ॥
तथा तस्यास्तदा जातौ नासत्यावश्विनावुभौ ॥ 85 ॥
1.106.m: Her two nostrils, O king, were filled then with his semen; / from that, the two Nāsatyas, the Aśvins, were born to her.

1.106.s:
bhūmau ca patitaṃ yacca tābhyāṃ śukraṃ vimarditam ..
tasmātsośvātsamutpannaḥ kumāraḥ sūryasannibhaḥ .. 86 ..
1.106.d:
भूमौ च पतितं यच्च ताभ्यां शुक्रं विमर्दितम् ॥
तस्मात्सोश्वात्समुत्पन्नः कुमारः सूर्यसन्निभः ॥ 86 ॥
1.106.m: And the semen that fell onto the ground was rubbed together by them; / from that [and] from the horse was born a youth resembling the sun.

1.106.s:
tataḥ svarūpamāsthāya devadevo'pi bhāskaraḥ ..
svarūpiṇīmathādāya saṃjñāṃ tāṃ svagṛhaṃ yayau .. 87 ..
1.106.d:
ततः स्वरूपमास्थाय देवदेवोऽपि भास्करः ॥
स्वरूपिणीमथादाय संज्ञां तां स्वगृहं ययौ ॥ 87 ॥
1.106.m: Then, assuming his own form, the god of gods, the sun, / took Saṃjñā, who had also resumed her own form, and went to his own home.

1.106.s:
nāsatyau devabhiṣajau kṛtavānaśvināvubhau ..
tato vimardanājjātaṃ putraṃ dṛṣṭvā divākaraḥ ..88..
1.106.d:
नासत्यौ देवभिषजौ कृतवानश्विनावुभौ ॥
ततो विमर्दनाज्जातं पुत्रं दृष्ट्वा दिवाकरः ॥88॥
1.106.m: He made both Aśvins, the Nāsatyas, the physicians of the gods. / Then, seeing the son born of the rubbing,

1.106.s:
revanteti tadā tasya nāma cakre jagadguruḥ ..
taṃ ca putramuvācāttha sūryo grahagaṇeśvaraḥ ..89..
1.106.d:
रेवन्तेति तदा तस्य नाम चक्रे जगद्गुरुः ॥
तं च पुत्रमुवाचात्थ सूर्यो ग्रहगणेश्वरः ॥89॥
1.106.m: the guru of the world named him Revanta. / And the sun, the lord of the hosts of planets, spoke to that son:

1.106.s:
yasmātso'śvātsamutpanno mattastva ddīptadīdhitiḥ ..
pūjāmāpsyasi so'śvebhyastasmānnityaṃ jagatpriyaḥ .. 1.106.90 ..
1.106.d:
यस्मात्सोऽश्वात्समुत्पन्नो मत्तस्त्व द्दीप्तदीधितिः ॥
पूजामाप्स्यसि सोऽश्वेभ्यस्तस्मान्नित्यं जगत्प्रियः ॥ 1.106.90 ॥
1.106.m: "Because you were born of a horse from me, O you of blazing splendour, / you will receive worship from horses and will ever be dear to the world.

1.106.s:
ye ca tvāṃ pūjayiṣyanti teṣāṃ vṛddhirbhaviṣyati ..
śanaiścarasya te janma mayoktaṃ nṛpasattama .. 91 ..
1.106.d:
ये च त्वां पूजयिष्यन्ति तेषां वृद्धिर्भविष्यति ॥
शनैश्चरस्य ते जन्म मयोक्तं नृपसत्तम ॥ 91 ॥
1.106.m: And those who worship you will prosper." / The birth of Śanaiścara has been related to you, O best of kings.

1.106.s:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi rāhorjanma tathānagha ..
dākṣāyaṇī siṃhikākhyā bhāryā vai kaśyapasya tu ..92..
1.106.d:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि राहोर्जन्म तथानघ ॥
दाक्षायणी सिंहिकाख्या भार्या वै कश्यपस्य तु ॥92॥
1.106.m: Hereafter I will speak of the birth of Rāhu, O sinless one. / A daughter of Dakṣa named Siṃhikā was the wife of Kaśyapa.

1.106.s:
akāle varayāmāsa bhartāraṃ tapasānvitam ..
bhagavanputrakāmāhaṃ taṃ prayaccha mamānagha..93..
1.106.d:
अकाले वरयामास भर्तारं तपसान्वितम् ॥
भगवन्पुत्रकामाहं तं प्रयच्छ ममानघ॥93॥
1.106.m: At an improper time, she solicited her husband who was endowed with austerities: / "O lord, I desire a son; grant him to me, O sinless one!"

1.106.s:
akālayañcāsaṃkruddhastāṃ jagāda sa kaśyapaḥ ..
daityadānavasaṃkāśaṃ putra tvaṃ janayiṣyasi..94..
1.106.d:
अकालयञ्चासंक्रुद्धस्तां जगाद स कश्यपः ॥
दैत्यदानवसंकाशं पुत्र त्वं जनयिष्यसि॥94॥
1.106.m: Enraged by the unseasonable request, Kaśyapa said to her: / "You will bear a son resembling Daityas and Dānavas."

1.106.s:
rāhuṃ sā janayāmāsa varadānānmahātmanaḥ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi ketoste janma pārthiva..95..
1.106.d:
राहुं सा जनयामास वरदानान्महात्मनः॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि केतोस्ते जन्म पार्थिव॥95॥
1.106.m: Through that boon of the great-souled one, she gave birth to Rāhu. / Hereafter I will relate the birth of Ketu to you, O king.

1.106.s:
prajānāṃ mahatīṃ vṛddhiṃ dṛṣṭvā devaḥ pitāmahaḥ ..
kṣaye tāsāṃ tadā cakre buddhiṃ buddhimatāṃ varaḥ .. 96 ..
1.106.d:
प्रजानां महतीं वृद्धिं दृष्ट्वा देवः पितामहः ॥
क्षये तासां तदा चक्रे बुद्धिं बुद्धिमतां वरः ॥ 96 ॥
1.106.m: Seeing the immense increase of creatures, the god, the grandfather, / the best among the wise, resolved upon their destruction.

1.106.s:
kṣayaṃ cintayatastasya prajānāṃ manujeśvara ..
prādurbhūtā tataḥ kanyā mṛtyurnāmeti viśrutā .. 97 ..
1.106.d:
क्षयं चिन्तयतस्तस्य प्रजानां मनुजेश्वर ॥
प्रादुर्भूता ततः कन्या मृत्युर्नामेति विश्रुता ॥ 97 ॥
1.106.m: As he was contemplating the destruction of creatures, O ruler of men, / there emerged a maiden widely renowned by the name Mṛtyu.

1.106.s:
tāṃ jagāda tadā brahmā prajāḥ saṃhara śobhane ..
sā tathoktā tadā tena ruroda varavarṇinī .. 98 ..
1.106.d:
तां जगाद तदा ब्रह्मा प्रजाः संहर शोभने ॥
सा तथोक्ता तदा तेन रुरोद वरवर्णिनी ॥ 98 ॥
1.106.m: Brahmā then said to her: "Destroy the creatures, O fair one." / Thus addressed by him, the woman of fair complexion wept.

1.106.s:
tadāśrubindubhirjātā vyādhayo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā vyādhīnsamutpannānsaṃhṛtyāśrūṇi bhāminī .. 99 ..
1.106.d:
तदाश्रुबिन्दुभिर्जाता व्याधयोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
दृष्ट्वा व्याधीन्समुत्पन्नान्संहृत्याश्रूणि भामिनी ॥ 99 ॥
1.106.m: From those teardrops, diseases arose by the thousands. / Seeing the diseases that had arisen, the passionate lady restrained her tears

1.106.s:
suduścaraṃ tapastepe puṣkarāraṇyamāśritā ..
sthāneṣu ca tathānyeṣu bahūnvarṣagaṇāñchubhā .. 1.106.100 ..
1.106.d:
सुदुश्चरं तपस्तेपे पुष्करारण्यमाश्रिता ॥
स्थानेषु च तथान्येषु बहून्वर्षगणाञ्छुभा ॥ 1.106.100 ॥
1.106.m: and, resorting to the forest of Puṣkara, the auspicious woman practiced very difficult austerities / there and in other places for many series of years.

1.106.s:
bhūyo jagāda tāṃ brahmā prajāḥ saṃhara śobhane ..
mayoktaṃ yatpurā bhadre tattathā na tadanyathā .. 101 ..
1.106.d:
भूयो जगाद तां ब्रह्मा प्रजाः संहर शोभने ॥
मयोक्तं यत्पुरा भद्रे तत्तथा न तदन्यथा ॥ 101 ॥
1.106.m: Brahmā said to her once more: "Destroy the creatures, O fair one; / what I have spoken previously, gentle lady, must be so and not otherwise.

1.106.s:
tapasā te varaṃ grāhyaṃ tadācakṣva suśobhane ..
nṛṇāṃ nimittaṃ maraṇe loke yāsyati doṣataḥ .. 102 ..
1.106.d:
तपसा ते वरं ग्राह्यं तदाचक्ष्व सुशोभने ॥
नृणां निमित्तं मरणे लोके यास्यति दोषतः ॥ 102 ॥
1.106.m: Choose a boon for your austerity; speak it, O very beautiful woman! / The cause for death will come upon men in the world due to fault;

1.106.s:
na kaściddoṣato mantā tvāṃ kadācidapi dhruve ..
evamuktā tadā tena brahmaṇā sā śubhānanā .103..
1.106.d:
न कश्चिद्दोषतो मन्ता त्वां कदाचिदपि ध्रुवे ॥
एवमुक्ता तदा तेन ब्रह्मणा सा शुभानना .103॥
1.106.m: no one will ever think of you as having any fault, O constant one." / Having been addressed thus by Brahmā, that woman of auspicious face

1.106.s:
dīrghamuṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvāsaṃ mumoca varavarṇinī..
kṛṣṇasarpasamākārastasmātketurajāyata.104..
1.106.d:
दीर्घमुष्णं च निःश्वासं मुमोच वरवर्णिनी॥
कृष्णसर्पसमाकारस्तस्मात्केतुरजायत.104॥
1.106.m: released a long and hot sigh, that lady of fair complexion; / from that Ketu was born, having the form of a black serpent,

1.106.s:
śikhidīptaśikho rājankālānalasamaprabhaḥ ..
dhūmaprabhasya tasyātha keturūpasya pārthiva .. 105 ..
1.106.d:
शिखिदीप्तशिखो राजन्कालानलसमप्रभः ॥
धूमप्रभस्य तस्याथ केतुरूपस्य पार्थिव ॥ 105 ॥
1.106.m: with a blazing crested top, O king, having a lustre like the fire of time. / Then to that Ketu-formed one of smoky lustre, O king,

1.106.s:
saṃjñāṃ cakāra sarvātmā devadevaḥ pitāmahaḥ ..
dhūmaketurayaṃ nāmnā bhaviṣyati jagattraye .. 106 ..
1.106.d:
संज्ञां चकार सर्वात्मा देवदेवः पितामहः ॥
धूमकेतुरयं नाम्ना भविष्यति जगत्त्रये ॥ 106 ॥
1.106.m: the god of gods, the grandfather, the universal soul, gave a name: / "He will be known by the name Dhūmaketu in the three worlds,

1.106.s:
darśayiṣyati lokānāṃ tathaiva ca śubhāśubham ..
divyantarikṣe bhuvi caika eṣaḥ sandṛśyate dhūmaketurmahātmā ..
saṃsthānarūpaistu bahuprakāraiḥ śubhāśubhaṃ darśayanmānuṣāṇām .. 107 ..
1.106.d:
दर्शयिष्यति लोकानां तथैव च शुभाशुभम् ॥
दिव्यन्तरिक्षे भुवि चैक एषः सन्दृश्यते धूमकेतुर्महात्मा ॥
संस्थानरूपैस्तु बहुप्रकारैः शुभाशुभं दर्शयन्मानुषाणाम् ॥ 107 ॥
1.106.m: and likewise he will show what is auspicious and inauspicious to the worlds." / In the sky, in the atmosphere, and on the earth, this one great-souled Dhūmaketu is seen, / displaying good and evil to mortals through forms of many kinds.

1.107.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
pūrvaṃ brahmā mahīpāla sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ ..
abhyayuṅkta tadātmānaṃ tasya yuktasya pārthiva .. 1 ..
1.107.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
पूर्वं ब्रह्मा महीपाल सिसृक्षुर्विविधाः प्रजाः ॥
अभ्ययुङ्क्त तदात्मानं तस्य युक्तस्य पार्थिव ॥ 1 ॥
1.107.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Formerly, O ruler of the earth, Brahmā, desiring to create diverse creatures, / concentrated himself then; as he was concentrated, O earthly king,

1.107.s:
tato'sya jaghanātpūrvamasurāñjajñire sutān ..
asuḥ prāṇaḥ smṛto vipraistajanmānastato'surāḥ ..2..
1.107.d:
ततोऽस्य जघनात्पूर्वमसुराञ्जज्ञिरे सुतान् ॥
असुः प्राणः स्मृतो विप्रैस्तजन्मानस्ततोऽसुराः ॥2॥
1.107.m: then first from his loins the asuras were born as sons. / 'Asu' is declared to be vital breath by the learned; from being born from that, they are asuras.

1.107.s:
yathā sṛṣṭāḥ surāstanvā tāṃ tanuṃ sovyapohata ..
avyaktaṃ tattvabahulaṃ tatastānsobhyayuñjata ..3..
1.107.d:
यथा सृष्टाः सुरास्तन्वा तां तनुं सोव्यपोहत ॥
अव्यक्तं तत्त्वबहुलं ततस्तान्सोभ्ययुञ्जत ॥3॥
1.107.m: When the suras were created by [another] body, he cast off that body. / Then, full of the unmanifest reality, he applied himself to them.

1.107.s:
tatastānyuñjamānasya priyamāsītprabhoḥ kila ..
tato mukhātsamutpannā divyatastasya devatāḥ .. 4 ..
1.107.d:
ततस्तान्युञ्जमानस्य प्रियमासीत्प्रभोः किल ॥
ततो मुखात्समुत्पन्ना दिव्यतस्तस्य देवताः ॥ 4 ॥
1.107.m: Then, as he was applying himself to them, it was pleasing to the Lord indeed; / then from his mouth, shining with light, the deities were born.

1.107.s:
utpannā divyatastasmāddevāstena tataḥ smṛtāḥ ..
dhāturdevīti yatproktaṃ krīḍārthaṃ saṃvibhāvyate ..5..
1.107.d:
उत्पन्ना दिव्यतस्तस्माद्देवास्तेन ततः स्मृताः ॥
धातुर्देवीति यत्प्रोक्तं क्रीडार्थं संविभाव्यते ॥5॥
1.107.m: Because they were born shining with light, therefore they are remembered as devas. / The verbal root 'div' is explained as meaning 'to play'.

1.107.s:
tasmāddevyāntu tanvāyāṃ jajñire tasya devatāḥ ..
devāndṛṣṭvā tataḥ so vai tanumanyāṃ prapadyata ..6 ..
1.107.d:
तस्माद्देव्यान्तु तन्वायां जज्ञिरे तस्य देवताः ॥
देवान्दृष्ट्वा ततः सो वै तनुमन्यां प्रपद्यत ॥6 ॥
1.107.m: Therefore, in that divine body, his deities were born. / Having seen the devas, he then assumed another body.

1.107.s:
sattvamātrātmikāmeva tanuṃ tāṃ so'bhyayuñjata ..
piteva manyamānastānsutānpravyādha sa prabhuḥ .. 7 ..
1.107.d:
सत्त्वमात्रात्मिकामेव तनुं तां सोऽभ्ययुञ्जत ॥
पितेव मन्यमानस्तान्सुतान्प्रव्याध स प्रभुः ॥ 7 ॥
1.107.m: He concentrated on that body consisting solely of sattva; / regarding them as sons, like a father, that Lord cast [it] aside.

1.107.s:
pitaro hyupapakṣābhyāṃ madhye rātryahnayoḥ purā ..
tasmātte pitaro devāḥ pitṛtvaṃ teṣu tatsmṛtam .. 8 ..
1.107.d:
पितरो ह्युपपक्षाभ्यां मध्ये रात्र्यह्नयोः पुरा ॥
तस्मात्ते पितरो देवाः पितृत्वं तेषु तत्स्मृतम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.107.m: The Pitṛs [arose] from his sides between night and day in the past; / therefore they are the devas known as Pitṛs; their status as fathers is recorded among them.

1.107.s:
yayā sṛṣṭāstu pitarastanuṃ tāṃ sa vyapohata ..
sāpaviddhā tanustena sadyaḥ saṃdhyā vyajāyata....
tasmādahardevatānāṃ rātriḥ syādāsurī matā ..
tayormadhye tu pitaraḥ sā tanustu garīyasī .. 1.107.10 ..
1.107.d:
यया सृष्टास्तु पितरस्तनुं तां स व्यपोहत ॥
सापविद्धा तनुस्तेन सद्यः संध्या व्यजायत॥॥
तस्मादहर्देवतानां रात्रिः स्यादासुरी मता ॥
तयोर्मध्ये तु पितरः सा तनुस्तु गरीयसी ॥ 1.107.10 ॥
1.107.m:
That body by which the Pitṛs were created he cast off; / that body abandoned by him instantly became twilight.
Therefore the day belongs to the deities, and the night is considered asurian; / but between the two are the Pitṛs; and that body is most weighty.

1.107.s:
tasmāddevāsurāścaiva ṛṣayo mānavāstathā ..
yuktāste tāmupāsante tathā viṣṇoryadantaram .. 11 ..
1.107.d:
तस्माद्देवासुराश्चैव ऋषयो मानवास्तथा ॥
युक्तास्ते तामुपासन्ते तथा विष्णोर्यदन्तरम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.107.m: Therefore both devas and asuras, and likewise ṛṣis and human beings, / focused [in mind], worship it, and likewise the interval of Viṣṇu.

1.107.s:
tasmādrātryahnayoḥ sandhāvupāsante dvijāstu tām ..
tato'nyasyāṃ punarbrahmā sa tanvāmupapadyata .. 12 ..
1.107.d:
तस्माद्रात्र्यह्नयोः सन्धावुपासन्ते द्विजास्तु ताम् ॥
ततोऽन्यस्यां पुनर्ब्रह्मा स तन्वामुपपद्यत ॥ 12 ॥
1.107.m: Therefore, at the twilight junction of night and day, the twice-born worship it. / Then again Brahmā assumed another body.

1.107.s:
rājasattvātmikāyāṃ tu manasā so'sṛjatprabhuḥ ..
manasā tu tatastasya prajānāñjajñire prajāḥ .. 13 ..
1.107.d:
राजसत्त्वात्मिकायां तु मनसा सोऽसृजत्प्रभुः ॥
मनसा तु ततस्तस्य प्रजानाञ्जज्ञिरे प्रजाः ॥ 13 ॥
1.107.m: In [the body] consisting of rajas and sattva, the Lord created with his mind. / Then by his mind, the offspring of creatures were born to him.

1.107.s:
manasā ca manuṣyāste jananātprathitāḥ prajāḥ ..
sṛṣṭvā punaḥ prajāḥ saumyasyāṃ tanuṃ so'vyapohata .. 14 ..
1.107.d:
मनसा च मनुष्यास्ते जननात्प्रथिताः प्रजाः ॥
सृष्ट्वा पुनः प्रजाः सौम्यस्यां तनुं सोऽव्यपोहत ॥ 14 ॥
1.107.m: Through mind (manas) they are human beings (manuṣya), renowned as offspring (prajā) because of birth (janana). / Having created the creatures again, he cast off that body of gentle nature.

1.107.s:
sāpaviddhā tanustena jyotsnā sadyaḥ prajāyata ..
tasmādbhavanti saṃhṛṣṭā jyotsnāyā udbhave prajāḥ .. 15 ..
1.107.d:
सापविद्धा तनुस्तेन ज्योत्स्ना सद्यः प्रजायत ॥
तस्माद्भवन्ति संहृष्टा ज्योत्स्नाया उद्भवे प्रजाः ॥ 15 ॥
1.107.m: That body abandoned by him instantly became moonlight. / Therefore creatures become delighted at the arising of moonlight.

1.107.s:
tāmutsṛjya tato jyotsnāṃ tato'nyā prāviśatpunaḥ ..
mūrtiṃ rajastamāsaktāṃ tatastāṃ sobhyayuñjata .. 16 ..
1.107.d:
तामुत्सृज्य ततो ज्योत्स्नां ततोऽन्या प्राविशत्पुनः ॥
मूर्तिं रजस्तमासक्तां ततस्तां सोभ्ययुञ्जत ॥ 16 ॥
1.107.m: Then, having cast aside that moonlight, he again entered another / form attached to rajas and tamas, and then concentrated on it.

1.107.s:
tato'nyāssāndhakāre tu kṣudhāviṣṭāḥ prajāḥ sṛjan ..
tāḥ sṛṣṭvā tu kṣudhāviṣṭā aṃgulyā dātumudyatāḥ .. 17 ..
1.107.d:
ततोऽन्यास्सान्धकारे तु क्षुधाविष्टाः प्रजाः सृजन् ॥
ताः सृष्ट्वा तु क्षुधाविष्टा अंगुल्या दातुमुद्यताः ॥ 17 ॥
1.107.m: Then, in deep darkness, he created other creatures overcome with hunger. / Having been created, overcome with hunger, they were eager to swallow [him] with their fingers.

1.107.s:
aṃbhāṃsyetāni rakṣāma uktavantastu teṣu ye ..
rākṣasāste smṛtāstasmātkṣudhātmāno niśācarāḥ .. 18 ..
1.107.d:
अंभांस्येतानि रक्षाम उक्तवन्तस्तु तेषु ये ॥
राक्षसास्ते स्मृतास्तस्मात्क्षुधात्मानो निशाचराः ॥ 18 ॥
1.107.m: Those among them who said, "Let us protect (rakṣāmaḥ) these waters," / were therefore known as rākṣasas, hungry-souled night-wanderers.

1.107.s:
dhruvaṃ kṣaṇomi yembhāṃsi teṣu dṛṣṭvā parasparam ..
tena te karmaṇā yakṣā guhyakāḥ krūrakarmiṇaḥ .. 19 ..
1.107.d:
ध्रुवं क्षणोमि येम्भांसि तेषु दृष्ट्वा परस्परम् ॥
तेन ते कर्मणा यक्षा गुह्यकाः क्रूरकर्मिणः ॥ 19 ॥
1.107.m: Seeing one another, those among them [who said], "I am surely destroying (kṣaṇomi) the waters"— / by that action they became yakṣas and guhyakas of cruel deeds.

1.107.s:
rakṣaṇe pālane cāpi dhātureva vibhāvyate ..
yakṣa ityeṣa dhāturvai kṣepaṇe sannirudhyate .. 1.107.20 ..
1.107.d:
रक्षणे पालने चापि धातुरेव विभाव्यते ॥
यक्ष इत्येष धातुर्वै क्षेपणे सन्निरुध्यते ॥ 1.107.20 ॥
1.107.m: The verbal root [rakṣ] is understood in the sense of protecting and guarding, / while this root yakṣ is defined in the sense of destroying.

1.107.s:
rakṣaṇādrakṣa ityuktāḥ kṣapaṇādyakṣa ucyate ..
tāndṛṣṭvā tatkṣaṇenāsya keśāḥ śīryanta dhīmataḥ .. 21 ..
1.107.d:
रक्षणाद्रक्ष इत्युक्ताः क्षपणाद्यक्ष उच्यते ॥
तान्दृष्ट्वा तत्क्षणेनास्य केशाः शीर्यन्त धीमतः ॥ 21 ॥
1.107.m: They are called rakṣas from protecting, and yakṣa is stated [to derive] from destroying. / Seeing them, at that moment the wise one's hairs fell out.

1.107.s:
te śīrṇā vyutthitā hyūrdhvamārohanta tataḥ punaḥ ..
sarpaṇāttu smṛtāḥ sarpāḥ pannatvātpannagāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 22 ..
1.107.d:
ते शीर्णा व्युत्थिता ह्यूर्ध्वमारोहन्त ततः पुनः ॥
सर्पणात्तु स्मृताः सर्पाः पन्नत्वात्पन्नगाः स्मृताः ॥ 22 ॥
1.107.m: Those fallen [hairs] rose upward and crawled again; / from crawling (sarpaṇa) they are called sarpa, and from creeping (panna) they are called pannaga.

1.107.s:
bālātmānaḥ smṛtā vyālā hīnatvāccāhayaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
pannatvātpannagāścāpi sarpāste'pāyasarpaṇāt .. 23 ..
1.107.d:
बालात्मानः स्मृता व्याला हीनत्वाच्चाहयः स्मृताः ॥
पन्नत्वात्पन्नगाश्चापि सर्पास्तेऽपायसर्पणात् ॥ 23 ॥
1.107.m: They are called vyāla because their nature is of hair (bāla), and ahi because of their deficiency; / and pannagas because of creeping, and sarpas because of crawling away.

1.107.s:
teṣāṃ layāḥ pṛthivyāpaḥ sūryācandramasau ghanāḥ ..
tasya krodho'bhavaddhūmamagnigarbhaḥ sudāruṇaḥ .. 24 ..
1.107.d:
तेषां लयाः पृथिव्यापः सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ घनाः ॥
तस्य क्रोधोऽभवद्धूममग्निगर्भः सुदारुणः ॥ 24 ॥
1.107.m: Their resting-places were the earth, waters, sun, moon, and clouds. / His anger became smoke containing fire, exceedingly terrible.

1.107.s:
sa tānsarpānsamutpannānāviveśa viṣātmakān ..
sarpāndṛṣṭvā tataḥ krodhatkrodhātmāno vinirmame .. 25 ..
1.107.d:
स तान्सर्पान्समुत्पन्नानाविवेश विषात्मकान् ॥
सर्पान्दृष्ट्वा ततः क्रोधत्क्रोधात्मानो विनिर्ममे ॥ 25 ॥
1.107.m: It entered those born serpents, venomous by nature. / Then, seeing the serpents, he created out of anger those whose nature is wrath.

1.107.s:
gāṃ dhayantastato dṛṣṭvā gandharvā agniretasaḥ ..
dhaya ityeṣa dhāturvai pāne hyeṣa nirudhyate .. 26 ..
1.107.d:
गां धयन्तस्ततो दृष्ट्वा गन्धर्वा अग्निरेतसः ॥
धय इत्येष धातुर्वै पाने ह्येष निरुध्यते ॥ 26 ॥
1.107.m: Then, seeing the gandharvas of fire-semen suckling the earth— / for the root dhā is indeed defined in the sense of drinking—

1.107.s:
pibanto jajñire vācā gandharvāstena te smṛtāḥ ..
karṇena kapilā bhūtvā piśācāḥ kapiśā hyalam .. 27 ..
1.107.d:
पिबन्तो जज्ञिरे वाचा गन्धर्वास्तेन ते स्मृताः ॥
कर्णेन कपिला भूत्वा पिशाचाः कपिशा ह्यलम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.107.m: as they were drinking with speech, they were born; therefore they are remembered as gandharvas. / Becoming tawny through the ear, piśācas were indeed very reddish-brown.

1.107.s:
bhūtatvātte smṛtā bhūtāḥ piśācāḥ piśitāśinaḥ ..
aṣṭāsu tāsu sṛṣṭāsu devayoniṣu sa prabhuḥ .. 28 ..
1.107.d:
भूतत्वात्ते स्मृता भूताः पिशाचाः पिशिताशिनः ॥
अष्टासु तासु सृष्टासु देवयोनिषु स प्रभुः ॥ 28 ॥
1.107.m: From their having been (bhūtatva), they are remembered as bhūtas, and piśācas from being flesh-eaters (piśitāśin). / When those eight divine wombs were created, that Lord

1.107.s:
tataḥ svacchandato'nyāni vayāṃsi vayasā sṛjan ..
pakṣiṇaḥ sa tu dṛṣṭvā vai tataḥ paśugaṇānsṛjan .. 29 ..
1.107.d:
ततः स्वच्छन्दतोऽन्यानि वयांसि वयसा सृजन् ॥
पक्षिणः स तु दृष्ट्वा वै ततः पशुगणान्सृजन् ॥ 29 ॥
1.107.m: then created other birds at will with his youthful vigor; / seeing the birds indeed, he then created the herds of animals.

1.107.s:
mukhato'jāḥ sṛjanso vai vakṣasaścā vayo'sṛjat ..
gāvaścaivodarādbrahmā punaranyām̐śca nirmame .. 1.107.30 ..
1.107.d:
मुखतोऽजाः सृजन्सो वै वक्षसश्चा वयोऽसृजत् ॥
गावश्चैवोदराद्ब्रह्मा पुनरन्याम्̐श्च निर्ममे ॥ 1.107.30 ॥
1.107.m: Creating goats from his mouth, he created sheep from his chest; / and cows from his belly, Brahmā created still others:

1.107.s:
pādato'śvāṃsturaṅgāṃśca rāsabhāngavayānmṛgān ..
uṣṭrāṃścaiva varāhāṃśca śvānānanyāṃśca jātayaḥ .. 31 ..
1.107.d:
पादतोऽश्वांस्तुरङ्गांश्च रासभान्गवयान्मृगान् ॥
उष्ट्रांश्चैव वराहांश्च श्वानानन्यांश्च जातयः ॥ 31 ॥
1.107.m: from his feet, horses and mounts, donkeys, wild oxen, and deer, / and camels, boars, dogs, and other species.

1.107.s:
oṣadhyaḥ phalamūlinyo romabhistasya jajñire ..
evaṃvidhauṣadhīḥ sṛṣṭvā nyayujatso'dhvareṣu tāḥ .. 32 ..
1.107.d:
ओषध्यः फलमूलिन्यो रोमभिस्तस्य जज्ञिरे ॥
एवंविधौषधीः सृष्ट्वा न्ययुजत्सोऽध्वरेषु ताः ॥ 32 ॥
1.107.m: Herbs with fruits and roots were born from his hair; / having created herbs of such kinds, he appointed them for sacrifices.

1.107.s:
asya tvādau tu kalpasya tretāyugamukhe purā ..
gaurajaḥ puruṣothāvirathāśvataragardabhāḥ .. 33 ..
1.107.d:
अस्य त्वादौ तु कल्पस्य त्रेतायुगमुखे पुरा ॥
गौरजः पुरुषोथाविरथाश्वतरगर्दभाः ॥ 33 ॥
1.107.m: At the beginning of this aeon, at the opening of the Tretā age in the past, / the cow, goat, horse, sheep, and mule and donkey—

1.107.s:
ete grāmyāḥ smṛtāḥ sapta āraṇyāḥ sapta cāpare ..
mahiṣo gavayoṣṭrāstu dvikhuraḥ śarabho dvipaḥ .. 34 ..
1.107.d:
एते ग्राम्याः स्मृताः सप्त आरण्याः सप्त चापरे ॥
महिषो गवयोष्ट्रास्तु द्विखुरः शरभो द्विपः ॥ 34 ॥
1.107.m: these seven are remembered as domestic animals; and there are seven wild ones: / the buffalo, the wild ox, camels, the cloven-hoofed, the śarabha, the elephant,

1.107.s:
markaṭaḥ saptamasteṣāmāraṇyāḥ paśavastu te ..
gāyatrīṃ ca ṛcaṃ caiva trivṛtstomaṃ rathantaram .. 35 ..
1.107.d:
मर्कटः सप्तमस्तेषामारण्याः पशवस्तु ते ॥
गायत्रीं च ऋचं चैव त्रिवृत्स्तोमं रथन्तरम् ॥ 35 ॥
1.107.m: and the monkey is the seventh of them; these are wild animals. / And the Gāyatrī, the Ṛg verse, the Trivṛt hymn, the Rathantara,

1.107.s:
agniṣṭomaṃ ca yajñānāṃ nirmame prathamānmukhāt ..
yajño'pi traiṣṭubhaṃ chandaḥ stomaṃ pañcadaśastathā .. 36 ..
1.107.d:
अग्निष्टोमं च यज्ञानां निर्ममे प्रथमान्मुखात् ॥
यज्ञोऽपि त्रैष्टुभं छन्दः स्तोमं पञ्चदशस्तथा ॥ 36 ॥
1.107.m: and the Agniṣṭoma among sacrifices he created from his first mouth; / also the sacrificial rite, the Triṣṭubh metre, and the Pañcadaśa hymn,

1.107.s:
bṛhatsāma tathoktaṃ ca dakṣiṇātso'sṛjanmukhāt ..
sāmāni jagatī caiva stomaṃ saptadaśaṃ tathā .. 37 ..
1.107.d:
बृहत्साम तथोक्तं च दक्षिणात्सोऽसृजन्मुखात् ॥
सामानि जगती चैव स्तोमं सप्तदशं तथा ॥ 37 ॥
1.107.m: and the Bṛhat-sāman thus mentioned he created from his southern mouth; / the Sāmans, the Jagatī, and the Saptadaśa hymn,

1.107.s:
vairūpyamatirātraṃ ca paścimātso'sṛjanmukhāt ..
atharvamekaviṃśaṃ ca triṣṭubvairājameva ca ..
apturyāmaṃ ca yajñānāṃ cottarātso'sṛjanmukhāt .. 38 ..
1.107.d:
वैरूप्यमतिरात्रं च पश्चिमात्सोऽसृजन्मुखात् ॥
अथर्वमेकविंशं च त्रिष्टुब्वैराजमेव च ॥
अप्तुर्यामं च यज्ञानां चोत्तरात्सोऽसृजन्मुखात् ॥ 38 ॥
1.107.m: the Vairūpya and the Atirātra he created from his western mouth; / and the Atharvan, the Ekaviṃśa, the Triṣṭubh, and the Vairāja, / and the Aptoryāma among sacrifices he created from his northern mouth,

1.107.s: vidyuto'śanimeghāṃśca rohitendradhanūṃṣi ca .. 39 ..
1.107.d: विद्युतोऽशनिमेघांश्च रोहितेन्द्रधनूंषि च ॥ 39 ॥
1.107.m: and lightnings, thunderbolts, clouds, rainbows, and Indra's bows.

1.107.s:
sṛṣṭvā catuṣṭayaṃ pūrvaṃ devarṣipitṛmānavān ..
tato'sṛjatsa bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca .. 1.107.40 ..
1.107.d:
सृष्ट्वा चतुष्टयं पूर्वं देवर्षिपितृमानवान् ॥
ततोऽसृजत्स भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च ॥ 1.107.40 ॥
1.107.m: Having first created the fourfold group—devas, ṛṣis, Pitṛs, and human beings— / he then created beings stationary and moving.

1.107.s:
sṛṣṭvā yakṣapiśācāṃśca gandharvāpsarasastathā ..
narakinnararakṣāṃsi vayaḥ paśumṛgoragān .. 41 ..
1.107.d:
सृष्ट्वा यक्षपिशाचांश्च गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्तथा ॥
नरकिन्नररक्षांसि वयः पशुमृगोरगान् ॥ 41 ॥
1.107.m: Having created yakṣas, piśācas, and gandharvas and apsarases, / humans, kinnaras, rakṣases, birds, cattle, wild beasts, and serpents,

1.107.s:
avyayaṃ ca vyayaṃ caiva dvayaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam ..
jarāyujaṃ cāṇḍajaṃ ca sasvedajamathodbhijam .. 42 ..
1.107.d:
अव्ययं च व्ययं चैव द्वयं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
जरायुजं चाण्डजं च सस्वेदजमथोद्भिजम् ॥ 42 ॥
1.107.m: both the imperishable and the perishable, stationary and moving, / the womb-born, the egg-born, the sweat-born, and the plant-born.

1.107.s:
bhūtagrāmaṃ saṃkṛtavāndevadevaścaturvidham ..
paśavaśca mṛgāścaiva vyālāścobhayatodataḥ .. 43 ..
1.107.d:
भूतग्रामं संकृतवान्देवदेवश्चतुर्विधम् ॥
पशवश्च मृगाश्चैव व्यालाश्चोभयतोदतः ॥ 43 ॥
1.107.m: The god of gods made the fourfold host of beings: / domesticated animals, wild beasts, and predators having two rows of teeth,

1.107.s:
rakṣāṃsi ca piśācāṃśca manuṣyāṃśca jarāyujāḥ ..
aṇḍajāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ sarpānakrānmatsyāṃśca kacchapān .. 42 ..
1.107.d:
रक्षांसि च पिशाचांश्च मनुष्यांश्च जरायुजाः ॥
अण्डजाः पक्षिणः सर्पानक्रान्मत्स्यांश्च कच्छपान् ॥ 42 ॥
1.107.m: and rakṣasas, piśācas, and humans are born from a womb; / egg-born are birds, serpents, crocodiles, fish, and tortoises,

1.107.s:
yāni caivaṃ prakārāṇi sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca ..
svedajaṃ daṃśamaśakayūkāmakṣikamatkuṇam.. 45 ..
1.107.d:
यानि चैवं प्रकाराणि स्थावराणि चराणि च ॥
स्वेदजं दंशमशकयूकामक्षिकमत्कुणम्॥ 45 ॥
1.107.m: and whatever beings of this kind are stationary or moving. / Sweat-born are gnats, mosquitoes, lice, flies, and bedbugs,

1.107.s:
ūṣmaṇaścopajāyante yaccānyatkiñcidīdṛśam ..
udbhijāstaravaḥ sarve bījakāṇḍaprarohiṇaḥ .. 46 ..
1.107.d:
ऊष्मणश्चोपजायन्ते यच्चान्यत्किञ्चिदीदृशम् ॥
उद्भिजास्तरवः सर्वे बीजकाण्डप्ररोहिणः ॥ 46 ॥
1.107.m: and whatever else of such kind is born from heat. / Plant-born are all trees that shoot up from seeds or stems,

1.107.s:
oṣadhyaḥ phalapākāntā bahupuṣpaphalopagāḥ ..
apuṣpāḥ phalavanto ye te vanaspatayaḥ smṛtā ..47..
1.107.d:
ओषध्यः फलपाकान्ता बहुपुष्पफलोपगाः ॥
अपुष्पाः फलवन्तो ये ते वनस्पतयः स्मृता ॥47॥
1.107.m: annual herbs ending with the ripening of fruits and bearing many flowers and fruits; / those which bear fruit without flowers are called vanaspatis;

1.107.s:
puṣpiṇaḥ phalinaścaiva vṛkṣāścobhayataḥ śubhāḥ ..
pratānāścaiva vallyaśca vīrudhaḥ parikīrtitāḥ..48..
1.107.d:
पुष्पिणः फलिनश्चैव वृक्षाश्चोभयतः शुभाः ॥
प्रतानाश्चैव वल्ल्यश्च वीरुधः परिकीर्तिताः॥48॥
1.107.m: auspicious trees are both flowering and fruit-bearing; / creepers and climbing plants are celebrated as vīrudhs;

1.107.s:
gucchagulmaṃ tu vividhaṃ tathaiva tṛṇajātayaḥ ..
bījakāṇḍaruhāṇyeva pratānā vallya eva ca .. 49 ..
1.107.d:
गुच्छगुल्मं तु विविधं तथैव तृणजातयः ॥
बीजकाण्डरुहाण्येव प्रताना वल्ल्य एव च ॥ 49 ॥
1.107.m: and various cluster-shrubs, and likewise kinds of grass, / which grow from seeds or stems, and climbing plants and creepers.

1.107.s:
tamasā bahurūpeṇa veṣṭitāḥ karmahetunā ..
anusaṃjñā bhavantyete sukhaduḥkhasamanvitāḥ .. 1.107.50 ..
1.107.d:
तमसा बहुरूपेण वेष्टिताः कर्महेतुना ॥
अनुसंज्ञा भवन्त्येते सुखदुःखसमन्विताः ॥ 1.107.50 ॥
1.107.m: Enveloped by darkness of manifold forms on account of their past actions, / these [plants] possess inner consciousness and experience pleasure and pain.

1.107.s:
ekadantāstu gatayo brahmādyāḥ samudāhṛtāḥ ..
ghore'sminbhūtasaṃsāre nitye satatayāyini .. 51 ..
1.107.d:
एकदन्तास्तु गतयो ब्रह्माद्याः समुदाहृताः ॥
घोरेऽस्मिन्भूतसंसारे नित्ये सततयायिनि ॥ 51 ॥
1.107.m: These destinies, beginning with Brahmā, are said to be uniform / in this dreadful, constant, and ever-moving cycle of living beings.

1.107.s:
yaṃ tu karmaṇi yasminsa nyayuṅkta prathamaṃ prabhuḥ ..
tattadeva svayaṃ tejo yujyamānaḥ punaḥpunaḥ .. 52 ..
1.107.d:
यं तु कर्मणि यस्मिन्स न्ययुङ्क्त प्रथमं प्रभुः ॥
तत्तदेव स्वयं तेजो युज्यमानः पुनःपुनः ॥ 52 ॥
1.107.m: Whatever action the Lord appointed [each creature] to at first, / to that very action its own power repeatedly attaches itself.

1.107.s:
hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharme ṛtānṛte ..
tadbhāvitā prapadyante tasmāttattasya rocate .. 53 ..
1.107.d:
हिंस्राहिंस्रे मृदुक्रूरे धर्माधर्मे ऋतानृते ॥
तद्भाविता प्रपद्यन्ते तस्मात्तत्तस्य रोचते ॥ 53 ॥
1.107.m: Whether harming or non-harming, gentle or cruel, dharma or adharma, truth or untruth— / imbued with that, they attain it; therefore that pleases each.

1.107.s:
yadyasya sodadātsarge sa tattatsvayamāviśat ..
yathartuliṅgānyṛtavaḥ svayameva tu paryaye .. 54 ..
1.107.d:
यद्यस्य सोददात्सर्गे स तत्तत्स्वयमाविशत् ॥
यथर्तुलिङ्गान्यृतवः स्वयमेव तु पर्यये ॥ 54 ॥
1.107.m: Whatever [nature] he gave to each at creation, each entered into that of its own accord, / just as the seasons enter their own seasonal characteristics of their own accord in their rotation,

1.107.s:
svānisvānyabhipadyante tathā karmāṇi dehinām ..
lokānāṃ tu viśuddhyarthaṃ mukhabāhūrupādataḥ .. 55..
1.107.d:
स्वानिस्वान्यभिपद्यन्ते तथा कर्माणि देहिनाम् ॥
लोकानां तु विशुद्ध्यर्थं मुखबाहूरुपादतः ॥ 55॥
1.107.m: so the actions of embodied beings attain [their forms]. / But for the purification of the worlds, from his mouth, arms, thighs, and feet,

1.107.s:
brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ vaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ ca niravartayat..
āsyādvai brāhmaṇā jātā bāhubhyāṃ kṣatriyāḥ śubhāḥ .. 56 ..
1.107.d:
ब्राह्मणं क्षत्रियं वैश्यं शूद्रं च निरवर्तयत्॥
आस्याद्वै ब्राह्मणा जाता बाहुभ्यां क्षत्रियाः शुभाः ॥ 56 ॥
1.107.m: he brought forth the brāhmaṇa, the kṣatriya, the vaiśya, and the śūdra. / From his mouth were born the brāhmaṇas, from his arms the auspicious kṣatriyas,

1.107.s:
ūrubhyāṃ ca viśaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ śūdraḥ padbhyāmajāyata ..
varṇānāmāśramāṇāṃ ca dharmaṃ cakre pṛthakpṛthak..57..
1.107.d:
ऊरुभ्यां च विशः सृष्टाः शूद्रः पद्भ्यामजायत ॥
वर्णानामाश्रमाणां च धर्मं चक्रे पृथक्पृथक्॥57॥
1.107.m: from his thighs the vaiśyas were created, and the śūdra was born from his feet. / And he established the dharma of the castes and life-stages separately.

1.107.s:
svadharme ca niviṣṭānāṃ sthānāni vyadadhātprabhuḥ ..
brahmalokaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ śākraṃ kṣattriyajanmanām ..58..
1.107.d:
स्वधर्मे च निविष्टानां स्थानानि व्यदधात्प्रभुः ॥
ब्रह्मलोकं ब्राह्मणानां शाक्रं क्षत्त्रियजन्मनाम् ॥58॥
1.107.m: And for those abiding in their own dharma, the Lord ordained their stations: / the world of Brahmā for brāhmaṇas, the realm of Śakra for those of kṣatriya birth,

1.107.s:
mārutaṃ ca viśāṃ sthānaṃ gāndharvaṃ śūdrajanmanām ..
brahmacārivratasthānāṃ brahmalokaṃ prajāpatiḥ .. 59..
1.107.d:
मारुतं च विशां स्थानं गान्धर्वं शूद्रजन्मनाम् ॥
ब्रह्मचारिव्रतस्थानां ब्रह्मलोकं प्रजापतिः ॥ 59॥
1.107.m: the realm of the Wind for vaiśyas, and the realm of the Gandharvas for those born as śūdras. / Prajāpati [ordained] the world of Brahmā for those abiding by the vow of studentship,

1.107.s:
prājāpatyaṃ gṛhasthānāṃ yathāvihitakāriṇām ..
sthānaṃ sapta ṛṣīṇāṃ ca tathaiva vanavāsinām .. 1.107.60 ..
1.107.d:
प्राजापत्यं गृहस्थानां यथाविहितकारिणाम् ॥
स्थानं सप्त ऋषीणां च तथैव वनवासिनाम् ॥ 1.107.60 ॥
1.107.m: the realm of Prajāpati for householders who act as prescribed, / and the station of the Seven Seers likewise for forest-dwellers,

1.107.s:
yatīnāmakṛtaṃ sthānaṃ yatrecchāgāmināṃ sadā ..
kṛtvā sa sūtrasaṃsthānaṃ prajāgarbhaṃ tu mānasam .. 61 ..
1.107.d:
यतीनामकृतं स्थानं यत्रेच्छागामिनां सदा ॥
कृत्वा स सूत्रसंस्थानं प्रजागर्भं तु मानसम् ॥ 61 ॥
1.107.m: and the uncreated realm for ascetics, who can go wherever they wish. / Having made the basic layout, a mental womb of offspring,

1.107.s:
athāsṛjatprajākartṝnmānasām̐stanayānprabhuḥ ..
dharmaṃ rudraṃ manuṃ caiva sanakaṃ ca sanandanam .. 62 ..
1.107.d:
अथासृजत्प्रजाकर्तॄन्मानसाम्̐स्तनयान्प्रभुः ॥
धर्मं रुद्रं मनुं चैव सनकं च सनन्दनम् ॥ 62 ॥
1.107.m: the Lord then created the mind-born sons who are makers of progeny: / Dharma, Rudra, Manu, and Sanaka and Sanandana,

1.107.s:
bhṛguṃ sanatkumāraṃ ca ruciṃ śraddhāṃ tathaiva ca ..
marīcimatryaṅgirasau pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum .. 63 ..
1.107.d:
भृगुं सनत्कुमारं च रुचिं श्रद्धां तथैव च ॥
मरीचिमत्र्यङ्गिरसौ पुलस्त्यं पुलहं क्रतुम् ॥ 63 ॥
1.107.m: Bhṛgu, Sanatkumāra, Ruci, and likewise Śraddhā, / Marīci, Atri and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,

1.107.s:
vasiṣṭhaṃ ca mahābhāgaṃ nāradaṃ ca mahāmunim ..
svabhāskarānbarhiṣadaḥ agniṣvāttāṃstathaiva ca .. 64 ..
1.107.d:
वसिष्ठं च महाभागं नारदं च महामुनिम् ॥
स्वभास्करान्बर्हिषदः अग्निष्वात्तांस्तथैव च ॥ 64 ॥
1.107.m: and the highly fortunate Vasiṣṭha, and Nārada the great sage, / and the radiant Barhiṣads and Agniṣvāttas,

1.107.s:
kravyādāṃścopahūtāṃśca ājyapāṃśca sukālinaḥ ..
ādyā mūrtivihīnāśca trayasteṣāṃ gaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 65 ..
1.107.d:
क्रव्यादांश्चोपहूतांश्च आज्यपांश्च सुकालिनः ॥
आद्या मूर्तिविहीनाश्च त्रयस्तेषां गणाः स्मृताः ॥ 65 ॥
1.107.m: and the Kravyāds, Upahūtas, Ājyapas, and Sukālins. / Their first three classes are regarded as formless,

1.107.s:
caramāste gaṇāsteṣāṃ kathitāstu samūrtayaḥ ..
mahābhūtaśarīrāṇi sṛṣṭavānsa tathaiva ca .. 66 ..
1.107.d:
चरमास्ते गणास्तेषां कथितास्तु समूर्तयः ॥
महाभूतशरीराणि सृष्टवान्स तथैव च ॥ 66 ॥
1.107.m: and their latter classes are spoken of as having form. / And likewise he created bodies composed of the gross elements.

1.107.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā prajāsargaṃ cāṃguṣṭhāddakṣiṇāttataḥ ..
sasarja dakṣaṃ bhagavānvāmāṃguṣṭhāttathaiva ca .. 67 ..
1.107.d:
एवं कृत्वा प्रजासर्गं चांगुष्ठाद्दक्षिणात्ततः ॥
ससर्ज दक्षं भगवान्वामांगुष्ठात्तथैव च ॥ 67 ॥
1.107.m: Having thus made the creation of progeny, from his right thumb / the Blessed Lord then emitted Dakṣa, and likewise from his left thumb

1.107.s:
sasarja bhāryāṃ tasyaiva devadevaḥ pitāmahaḥ ..
tasyāṃ tu janayāmāsa dakṣo duhitaraḥ śubhāḥ ..68..
1.107.d:
ससर्ज भार्यां तस्यैव देवदेवः पितामहः ॥
तस्यां तु जनयामास दक्षो दुहितरः शुभाः ॥68॥
1.107.m: the god of gods, the Grandfather, emitted his wife. / Upon her, Dakṣa begot auspicious daughters,

1.107.s:
dadau tāśca sa dharmātmā brahmaputrebhya eva ca ..
satīṃ dadau sa rudrāya rudrā yasyāḥ sutāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 69 ..
1.107.d:
ददौ ताश्च स धर्मात्मा ब्रह्मपुत्रेभ्य एव च ॥
सतीं ददौ स रुद्राय रुद्रा यस्याः सुताः स्मृताः ॥ 69 ॥
1.107.m: and that righteous-minded one gave them to the sons of Brahmā. / He gave Satī to Rudra; from her, the Rudras are remembered as sons,

1.107.s:
asaṃkhyeyā mahāvīryā haratulyaparākramāḥ ..
yairvyāptaṃ bhuvanaṃ sarvaṃ sūryasyeva gabhastibhiḥ ..1.107.70..
1.107.d:
असंख्येया महावीर्या हरतुल्यपराक्रमाः ॥
यैर्व्याप्तं भुवनं सर्वं सूर्यस्येव गभस्तिभिः ॥1.107.70॥
1.107.m: innumerable, of great vigor, whose prowess is equal to Hara, / by whom the entire world is pervaded, as by the rays of the sun.

1.107.s:
bhṛgave ca dadau khyātiṃ rūpe ṇāpratimāṃ śubhām ..
bhṛgurdhātāvidhātārau janayāmāsa sāyudhau .. 71 ..
1.107.d:
भृगवे च ददौ ख्यातिं रूपे णाप्रतिमां शुभाम् ॥
भृगुर्धाताविधातारौ जनयामास सायुधौ ॥ 71 ॥
1.107.m: And he gave Khyāti, auspicious and peerless in beauty, to Bhṛgu. / Bhṛgu begot Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ, who bear weapons,

1.107.s:
śriyaṃ ca janayāmāsa khacarām̐śca turaṅgamān ..
bhṛguḥ prādācchriyaṃ devīṃ rājannārāyaṇasya ca..72..
1.107.d:
श्रियं च जनयामास खचराम्̐श्च तुरङ्गमान् ॥
भृगुः प्रादाच्छ्रियं देवीं राजन्नारायणस्य च॥72॥
1.107.m: and he begot Śrī and sky-faring horses. / Bhṛgu gave goddess Śrī, O king, to Nārāyaṇa;

1.107.s:
tasyāṃ saṃjanayāmāsa balonmādau madotkaṭau ..
meroḥ parvatarājasya dve kanye bhuvi viśrute..73..
1.107.d:
तस्यां संजनयामास बलोन्मादौ मदोत्कटौ ॥
मेरोः पर्वतराजस्य द्वे कन्ये भुवि विश्रुते॥73॥
1.107.m: upon her he begot Bala and Unmāda, who are vehement with passion. / The two daughters of Meru, king of mountains, renowned on earth,

1.107.s:
dhāturvidhātuste datte āyatirniyatistathā..
āyatirjanayāmāsa prāṇaṃ yadukulodvaha..74..
1.107.d:
धातुर्विधातुस्ते दत्ते आयतिर्नियतिस्तथा॥
आयतिर्जनयामास प्राणं यदुकुलोद्वह॥74॥
1.107.m: namely Āyati and Niyati, were given to Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ. / Āyati gave birth to Prāṇa, O descendant of the Yadu lineage,

1.107.s:
niyatirjanayāmāsa mṛkaṇḍuṃ tapasāṃ nidhim..
vyatīte saptame kalpe mṛkaṇḍoḥ sumahātmanaḥ... ..75..
1.107.d:
नियतिर्जनयामास मृकण्डुं तपसां निधिम्॥
व्यतीते सप्तमे कल्पे मृकण्डोः सुमहात्मनः॥॥.75॥
1.107.m: and Niyati gave birth to Mṛkaṇḍu, a storehouse of ascetic austerities. / When the seventh aeon had passed, from high-souled Mṛkaṇḍu,

1.107.s:
ahaṃ putraḥ samutpanno manasvinyāṃ narādhipa ..
patnī marīcessaṃbhūtirdakṣasya tanayā śubhā ..76..
1.107.d:
अहं पुत्रः समुत्पन्नो मनस्विन्यां नराधिप ॥
पत्नी मरीचेस्संभूतिर्दक्षस्य तनया शुभा ॥76॥
1.107.m: I was born as a son to Manasvinī, O ruler of men! / The wife of Marīci was Saṃbhūti, the auspicious daughter of Dakṣa;

1.107.s:
prajāpatiṃ pūrṇamāsaṃ janayāmāsa bhāminī ..
pūrṇamāsasya virajāḥ sudāmā tu tadātmajaḥ .. 77 ..
1.107.d:
प्रजापतिं पूर्णमासं जनयामास भामिनी ॥
पूर्णमासस्य विरजाः सुदामा तु तदात्मजः ॥ 77 ॥
1.107.m: that lady gave birth to Prajāpati Pūrṇamāsa. / Virajas was the son of Pūrṇamāsa, and Sudāman was his son,

1.107.s:
lokālokaniviṣṭastu lokapālo mayeritaḥ ..
putraśca paurṇamāsasya sarveśo nāma cāparaḥ .. 78 ..
1.107.d:
लोकालोकनिविष्टस्तु लोकपालो मयेरितः ॥
पुत्रश्च पौर्णमासस्य सर्वेशो नाम चापरः ॥ 78 ॥
1.107.m: who resides at Lokāloka, declared by me to be a world-guardian; / and another son of Paurṇamāsa was named Sarveśa.

1.107.s:
janayāmāsa putrau dvau stambaḥ kaśyapa eva ca ..
tayorgotrakarau putrau jñeyau saṃnyāsaniścayau .. 79 ..
1.107.d:
जनयामास पुत्रौ द्वौ स्तम्बः कश्यप एव च ॥
तयोर्गोत्रकरौ पुत्रौ ज्ञेयौ संन्यासनिश्चयौ ॥ 79 ॥
1.107.m: He begot two sons: Stamba and Kaśyapa. / The sons who established their lineages are to be known as resolute in renunciation.

1.107.s:
smṛtimaṅgirasaṃ prādāddakṣaḥ pūrvaṃ prajāpatiḥ ..
sinīvālī kuhū rākā tathaivānumatiḥ śubhā .. 1.107.80 ..
1.107.d:
स्मृतिमङ्गिरसं प्रादाद्दक्षः पूर्वं प्रजापतिः ॥
सिनीवाली कुहू राका तथैवानुमतिः शुभा ॥ 1.107.80 ॥
1.107.m: Earlier, Prajāpati Dakṣa gave Smṛti to Aṅgiras; / [from her were born] Sinīvālī, Kuhū, Rākā, and auspicious Anumati;

1.107.s:
tasyāṃ saṃjanayāmāsa agniṃ ca bharataṃ tathā ..
bharatasya tathā putraḥ parjanya iti viśrutaḥ .. 81 ..
1.107.d:
तस्यां संजनयामास अग्निं च भरतं तथा ॥
भरतस्य तथा पुत्रः पर्जन्य इति विश्रुतः ॥ 81 ॥
1.107.m: upon her he also begot Agni and Bharata. / And the son of Bharata is celebrated as Parjanya.

1.107.s:
hiraṇyaromā parjanya udīcīṃ diśamāśritaḥ ..
lokāloke'vatiṣṭham̐ste lokapālo mayeritaḥ .. 82 ..
1.107.d:
हिरण्यरोमा पर्जन्य उदीचीं दिशमाश्रितः ॥
लोकालोकेऽवतिष्ठम्̐स्ते लोकपालो मयेरितः ॥ 82 ॥
1.107.m: Golden-haired Parjanya has resorted to the northern direction; / residing at Lokāloka, he is declared by me to be a world-guardian.

1.107.s:
anusūyāṃ dadau dakṣaḥ tathātreḥ sumahātmanaḥ ..
tasyāṃ sa janayāmāsa taporāśikaraṃ param .. 83 ..
1.107.d:
अनुसूयां ददौ दक्षः तथात्रेः सुमहात्मनः ॥
तस्यां स जनयामास तपोराशिकरं परम् ॥ 83 ॥
1.107.m: Dakṣa gave Anusūyā likewise to high-souled Atri; / upon her he begot an eminent mass of ascetic power.

1.107.s:
prītiṃ dakṣaḥ pulastyāya dattorṇāṃ jananīṃ dadau ..
pulastyā kṣamāṃm prādātkardamasya tu mātaram .. 84 ..
1.107.d:
प्रीतिं दक्षः पुलस्त्याय दत्तोर्णां जननीं ददौ ॥
पुलस्त्या क्षमांम् प्रादात्कर्दमस्य तु मातरम् ॥ 84 ॥
1.107.m: Dakṣa gave Prīti to Pulastya, and gave Dattorṇā as mother; / Pulastya gave Kṣamā, the mother of Kardama.

1.107.s:
kārdamiḥ śaṅkhapādaśca dakṣiṇāmāśrito diśam ..
lokālokaniviṣṭaste lokapālo mayeritaḥ .. 85 ..
1.107.d:
कार्दमिः शङ्खपादश्च दक्षिणामाश्रितो दिशम् ॥
लोकालोकनिविष्टस्ते लोकपालो मयेरितः ॥ 85 ॥
1.107.m: Śaṅkhapāda, son of Kardama, has resorted to the southern direction; / residing at Lokāloka, he is declared by me to be a world-guardian.

1.107.s:
dakṣaśca sannatiṃ prādātkratave bhūritejase ..
ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi vālakhilyā iti smṛtāḥ .. 86 ..
1.107.d:
दक्षश्च सन्नतिं प्रादात्क्रतवे भूरितेजसे ॥
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि वालखिल्या इति स्मृताः ॥ 86 ॥
1.107.m: And Dakṣa gave Sannati to Kratu of great splendor; / their sixty thousand sons are known as the Vālakhilyas.

1.107.s:
janayāmāsa dharmajñānsarvāṃ stānūrdhvaretasaḥ ..
dakṣaḥ prādādarthevorṇāṃ vasiṣṭhāya mahātmane .. 87 ..
1.107.d:
जनयामास धर्मज्ञान्सर्वां स्तानूर्ध्वरेतसः ॥
दक्षः प्रादादर्थेवोर्णां वसिष्ठाय महात्मने ॥ 87 ॥
1.107.m:
He begot those [sons], all of whom knew dharma and had their semen drawn up.
Dakṣa gave Ūrṇā as a wife to the great-souled Vasiṣṭha.

1.107.s:
tasyāmasya sutā jātāḥ sapta saptāśvavarcasaḥ ..
rajobāhurūrdhvabāhuḥ pavanaścānaghaśca yaḥ .. 88 ..
1.107.d:
तस्यामस्य सुता जाताः सप्त सप्ताश्ववर्चसः ॥
रजोबाहुरूर्ध्वबाहुः पवनश्चानघश्च यः ॥ 88 ॥
1.107.m:
Upon her were born his seven sons, who had the splendour of the seven-horsed [sun]:
Rajobāhu, Ūrdhvabāhu, Pavana, and Anagha,

1.107.s:
sutapāḥ śaktirityete vāsiṣṭhāḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ ..
ketumānsumahātejā rājasaśca tathā sutaḥ .. 89 ..
1.107.d:
सुतपाः शक्तिरित्येते वासिष्ठाः सप्त कीर्तिताः ॥
केतुमान्सुमहातेजा राजसश्च तथा सुतः ॥ 89 ॥
1.107.m:
Sutapas, and Śakti—these are proclaimed as the seven Vāsiṣṭhas.
Ketumat of exceedingly great splendour, born of Rajas, is also his son;

1.107.s:
lokālokanivāsī te pratīcyāṃ sa mayeritaḥ ..
svāhāṃ prādātsa dakṣo'pi saśarīrāya vahnaye .. 90 ..
1.107.d:
लोकालोकनिवासी ते प्रतीच्यां स मयेरितः ॥
स्वाहां प्रादात्स दक्षोऽपि सशरीराय वह्नये ॥ 90 ॥
1.107.m:
Dwelling on the Lokāloka [mountain] in the west, he has been spoken of by me to you.
That Dakṣa also gave Svāhā to Fire in bodily form,

1.107.s:
divyāntarikṣabhaumānāmagnīnāṃ jananīṃ prabhuḥ ..
svadhāṃ prādātpitṛbhyastu menāyā jananīṃ śubhām .. 91 ..
1.107.d:
दिव्यान्तरिक्षभौमानामग्नीनां जननीं प्रभुः ॥
स्वधां प्रादात्पितृभ्यस्तु मेनाया जननीं शुभाम् ॥ 91 ॥
1.107.m:
The lord [gave] the mother of the celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial fires.
And he gave Svadhā, the auspicious mother of Menā, to the ancestors.

1.107.s:
himācalāya menāpi pitṛbhiḥ pratipāditā ..
caturdaśemāḥ kanyāśca dakṣo dharmāya vai dadau .. 1.107.90 ..
1.107.d:
हिमाचलाय मेनापि पितृभिः प्रतिपादिता ॥
चतुर्दशेमाः कन्याश्च दक्षो धर्माय वै ददौ ॥ 1.107.90 ॥
1.107.m:
Menā too was bestowed by the ancestors upon the Himālaya.
And these fourteen maidens Dakṣa indeed gave to Dharma:

1.107.s:
kītirlakṣmīrdhṛtirmedhā puṣṭiḥ śraddhā kriyā matiḥ ..
buddhirlajjā vapuḥ śāntiḥ tuṣṭiḥ siddhiścaturdaśa .. 93 ..
1.107.d:
कीतिर्लक्ष्मीर्धृतिर्मेधा पुष्टिः श्रद्धा क्रिया मतिः ॥
बुद्धिर्लज्जा वपुः शान्तिः तुष्टिः सिद्धिश्चतुर्दश ॥ 93 ॥
1.107.m:
Kīrti, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Medhā, Puṣṭi, Śraddhā, Kriyā, Mati,
Buddhi, Lajjā, Vapuḥ, Śānti, Tuṣṭi, and Siddhi are the fourteen.

1.107.s:
kīrtiputro yaśodevo darpo lakṣmīsutaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
niścayaśca dhṛteḥ putro medhāputrastathā śrutaḥ .. 94 ..
1.107.d:
कीर्तिपुत्रो यशोदेवो दर्पो लक्ष्मीसुतः स्मृतः ॥
निश्चयश्च धृतेः पुत्रो मेधापुत्रस्तथा श्रुतः ॥ 94 ॥
1.107.m:
The son of Kīrti is the god Yaśas; Darpa is remembered as the son of Lakṣmī;
Niścaya is the son of Dhṛti, and Śruta is likewise the son of Medhā;

1.107.s:
puṣṭirlābhaḥ sutaścaiva kāmaḥ śraddhāsutaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
kriyāyāstanayo devo matiputrastathā damaḥ .. 95 ..
1.107.d:
पुष्टिर्लाभः सुतश्चैव कामः श्रद्धासुतः स्मृतः ॥
क्रियायास्तनयो देवो मतिपुत्रस्तथा दमः ॥ 95 ॥
1.107.m:
The son of Puṣṭi is Lābha, and Kāma is remembered as the son of Śraddhā;
The son of Kriyā is Deva, and Dama is the son of Mati;

1.107.s:
buddherbodhaḥ sutaḥ prokto lajjāyā vinayaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
vapuṣo vyavasāyastu kṣemaḥ śāntisutastathā .. 95 ..
1.107.d:
बुद्धेर्बोधः सुतः प्रोक्तो लज्जाया विनयः स्मृतः ॥
वपुषो व्यवसायस्तु क्षेमः शान्तिसुतस्तथा ॥ 95 ॥
1.107.m:
Bodha is declared the son of Buddhi; Vinaya is remembered as [the son] of Lajjā;
Vyavasāya is [the son] of Vapus, and Kṣema is the son of Śānti;

1.107.s:
tuṣṭeḥ putrastu santoṣaḥ sukhaḥ siddheśca bhāsvaraḥ ..
kāmasya ca ratirbhāryā tatputro harṣa ucyate .. 97 ..
1.107.d:
तुष्टेः पुत्रस्तु सन्तोषः सुखः सिद्धेश्च भास्वरः ॥
कामस्य च रतिर्भार्या तत्पुत्रो हर्ष उच्यते ॥ 97 ॥
1.107.m:
The son of Tuṣṭi is Santoṣa, and the son of Siddhi is the radiant Sukha.
And Rati is the wife of Kāma; their son is called Harṣa.

1.107.s:
evaṃ prajāvivṛddhyarthaṃ dakṣo dattvā'tha kanyakāḥ ..
īje kadācidyajñena hayamedhena pārthiva .. 98 ..
1.107.d:
एवं प्रजाविवृद्ध्यर्थं दक्षो दत्त्वाऽथ कन्यकाः ॥
ईजे कदाचिद्यज्ञेन हयमेधेन पार्थिव ॥ 98 ॥
1.107.m:
Having thus given away his daughters for the increase of progeny,
Dakṣa once performed a sacrifice with a horse sacrifice, O king.

1.107.s:
tasya jāmātaraḥ sarve gatā yajñanimantritāḥ ..
bhāryābhiḥ sahitāḥ sarve rudraṃ devaṃ satīṃ vinā .. 99 ..
1.107.d:
तस्य जामातरः सर्वे गता यज्ञनिमन्त्रिताः ॥
भार्याभिः सहिताः सर्वे रुद्रं देवं सतीं विना ॥ 99 ॥
1.107.m:
All his sons-in-law, invited to the sacrifice, went there
Together with their wives, except for the god Rudra and Satī.

1.107.s:
rudro natiṃ na kurute bhāvyarthavinicoditaḥ ..
kadācidapi dakṣaśca tenāsau na nimantritaḥ .. 1.107.100 ..
1.107.d:
रुद्रो नतिं न कुरुते भाव्यर्थविनिचोदितः ॥
कदाचिदपि दक्षश्च तेनासौ न निमन्त्रितः ॥ 1.107.100 ॥
1.107.m:
Impelled by what was destined to be, Rudra would never bow
To Dakṣa; on that account he was not invited.

1.107.s:
anāhūtāpi ca gatā paścāttatra satī śubhā ..
dakṣānna lebhe pūjāṃ sā tataḥ kruddhā śubhānanā .. 101 ..
1.107.d:
अनाहूतापि च गता पश्चात्तत्र सती शुभा ॥
दक्षान्न लेभे पूजां सा ततः क्रुद्धा शुभानना ॥ 101 ॥
1.107.m:
Though uninvited, the auspicious Satī went there afterwards;
She received no honour from Dakṣa, and therefore, fair-faced, she became enraged.

1.107.s:
tatyāja dakṣasambhūtāṃ tāṃ tanuṃ himakandare ..
vinaṣṭāṃ tu satīṃ śrutvā devadevaḥ pinākadhṛk .. 102 ..
1.107.d:
तत्याज दक्षसम्भूतां तां तनुं हिमकन्दरे ॥
विनष्टां तु सतीं श्रुत्वा देवदेवः पिनाकधृक् ॥ 102 ॥
1.107.m:
She abandoned that body born of Dakṣa in a cave of the Himālaya.
Hearing that Satī had perished, the god of gods, the wielder of the Pināka,

1.107.s:
śaśāpa dakṣaṃ dharmajñaṃ manuṣyastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi ..
dhruvasyānvayasaṃbhūto rājā trailokyaviśrutaḥ .. 103 ..
1.107.d:
शशाप दक्षं धर्मज्ञं मनुष्यस्त्वं भविष्यसि ॥
ध्रुवस्यान्वयसंभूतो राजा त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतः ॥ 103 ॥
1.107.m:
Cursed Dakṣa, who knew dharma: 'You shall become a mortal man,
A king born in the lineage of Dhruva, renowned in the three worlds.

1.107.s:
tatrāpi vighnaṃ kartāsmi yajñakarmaṇyupasthite ..
bhṛguṃ marīcimatriṃ ca pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum .. 104 ..
1.107.d:
तत्रापि विघ्नं कर्तास्मि यज्ञकर्मण्युपस्थिते ॥
भृगुं मरीचिमत्रिं च पुलस्त्यं पुलहं क्रतुम् ॥ 104 ॥
1.107.m:
There too I shall cause an obstacle when the sacrificial rite is at hand.'
To Bhṛgu, Marīci, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,

1.107.s:
śaśāpa caivāṅgirasaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca mahāmunim ..
satīmanupravṛttasya dakṣasyāsya prajāpateḥ .. 105 ..
1.107.d:
शशाप चैवाङ्गिरसं वसिष्ठं च महामुनिम् ॥
सतीमनुप्रवृत्तस्य दक्षस्यास्य प्रजापतेः ॥ 105 ॥
1.107.m:
And to Aṅgiras, and to the great sage Vasiṣṭha he also pronounced a curse:
'Since this Prajāpati Dakṣa acted against Satī,

1.107.s:
anuvṛttiḥ kṛtā yasmādbhavadbhirdharmakovidaiḥ..
tasmādvaivasvate prāpte śubhe manvantare dvijāḥ .. 106 ..
1.107.d:
अनुवृत्तिः कृता यस्माद्भवद्भिर्धर्मकोविदैः॥
तस्माद्वैवस्वते प्राप्ते शुभे मन्वन्तरे द्विजाः ॥ 106 ॥
1.107.m:
And adherence [to him] was made by you who are skilled in dharma,
Therefore, O twice-born, when the auspicious Vaivasvata Manvantara has arrived,

1.107.s:
brahmaṇo yajamānasya janma krūramavāpsyatha ..
dehatyāge kṛte rājansatī devī mahābalā .. 107 ..
1.107.d:
ब्रह्मणो यजमानस्य जन्म क्रूरमवाप्स्यथ ॥
देहत्यागे कृते राजन्सती देवी महाबला ॥ 107 ॥
1.107.m:
You shall obtain a cruel birth from Brahmā as he sacrifices.'
When she had abandoned her body, O king, the goddess Satī of great power

1.107.s:
umeti viśrutā loke menāyāḥ samapadyata ..
himācalo'pi tāṃ devīṃ dadau śarvāya pārthiva .. .. 108 ..
1.107.d:
उमेति विश्रुता लोके मेनायाः समपद्यत ॥
हिमाचलोऽपि तां देवीं ददौ शर्वाय पार्थिव ॥ ॥ 108 ॥
1.107.m:
Was born to Menā, renowned in the world as Umā.
The Himālaya also gave that goddess to Śarva, O ruler of the earth.

1.107.s:
tayā viyujyate nāsau kadācidapi viśrutā ..
tasyāṃ tu janayāmāsa devadevo'pi śaṅkaraḥ .. 109 ..
1.107.d:
तया वियुज्यते नासौ कदाचिदपि विश्रुता ॥
तस्यां तु जनयामास देवदेवोऽपि शङ्करः ॥ 109 ॥
1.107.m:
He is never separated from her, the renowned one.
And upon her, Śaṅkara, the god of gods, begot

1.107.s:
vināyakaṃ kumāraṃ ca bhṛṅgeśaṃ sumahābalam ..
vighnānāṃ ca gaṇānāṃ ca putraṃ rājye'bhyaṣecayat .. 1.107.110 ..
1.107.d:
विनायकं कुमारं च भृङ्गेशं सुमहाबलम् ॥
विघ्नानां च गणानां च पुत्रं राज्येऽभ्यषेचयत् ॥ 1.107.110 ॥
1.107.m:
Vināyaka, Kumāra, and the exceedingly mighty Bhṛṅgeśa.
And he consecrated his son over the kingdom of obstacles and of the hosts—

1.107.s:
vināyakaṃ mahādevo gajavaktraṃ manasvinam ..
devasenāpatiṃ śakraḥ kumāraṃ kṛtavām̐stadā .. 111 ..
1.107.d:
विनायकं महादेवो गजवक्त्रं मनस्विनम् ॥
देवसेनापतिं शक्रः कुमारं कृतवाम्̐स्तदा ॥ 111 ॥
1.107.m:
The wise, elephant-faced Vināyaka did Mahādeva [consecrate].
Śakra then made Kumāra the general of the army of the gods,

1.107.s:
na tatyāja samīpācca bhṛṃgeśaṃ śaṅkarastadā ..
vaivasvatentare prāpte rājā dakṣo vyajāyata .. 112 ..
1.107.d:
न तत्याज समीपाच्च भृंगेशं शङ्करस्तदा ॥
वैवस्वतेन्तरे प्राप्ते राजा दक्षो व्यजायत ॥ 112 ॥
1.107.m:
And Śaṅkara then did not let Bhṛṅgeśa leave his side.
When the Vaivasvata interval arrived, Dakṣa was born as a king,

1.107.s:
dhruvasyānvayasambhūto mahābalaparākramaḥ ..
tatrāśvamedhe vitate anāhūtena śūlinā .. 113 ..
1.107.d:
ध्रुवस्यान्वयसम्भूतो महाबलपराक्रमः ॥
तत्राश्वमेधे वितते अनाहूतेन शूलिना ॥ 113 ॥
1.107.m:
Born in the lineage of Dhruva, endowed with great strength and prowess.
There, when a horse sacrifice was undertaken, by the spear-wielder, uninvited,

1.107.s:
yajño vidhvaṃsitastasya vīrabhadreṇa pārthiva ..
sa dakṣo janayāmāsa kanyāḥ pārthivasattama .. 114 ..
1.107.d:
यज्ञो विध्वंसितस्तस्य वीरभद्रेण पार्थिव ॥
स दक्षो जनयामास कन्याः पार्थिवसत्तम ॥ 114 ॥
1.107.m:
His sacrifice was destroyed by Vīrabhadra, O ruler of the earth.
That Dakṣa begot daughters, O best of rulers of the earth,

1.107.s:
tāsāṃ ca madhyātpradadāvaṣṭāviṃśatimindave ..
devatāstvabhimāninyo nakṣatrāṇāṃ pṛthakpṛthak .. 115 ..
1.107.d:
तासां च मध्यात्प्रददावष्टाविंशतिमिन्दवे ॥
देवतास्त्वभिमानिन्यो नक्षत्राणां पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 115 ॥
1.107.m:
And from among them he gave twenty-eight to the Moon,
Presiding deities of the lunar mansions, each distinct.

1.107.s:
uktaṃ hi te ṛkṣa gaṇasya janma śubhāvahaṃ pāpabhayāpahaṃ ca ..
ataḥ paraṃ kiṃ kathayāmi tubhyaṃ tattvaṃ vadasvāyatalohitākṣa ..116..
iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare prathamakhaṇḍe mā0 saṃ0 graharkṣādisaṃbhavādhyāyo nāma saptottaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..107 .. ..
1.107.d:
उक्तं हि ते ऋक्ष गणस्य जन्म शुभावहं पापभयापहं च ॥
अतः परं किं कथयामि तुभ्यं तत्त्वं वदस्वायतलोहिताक्ष ॥116॥
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे प्रथमखण्डे मा0 सं0 ग्रहर्क्षादिसंभवाध्यायो नाम सप्तोत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ॥107 ॥ ॥
1.107.m:
The birth of the host of lunar mansions has indeed been spoken to you, bringing auspiciousness and removing sin and fear.
What further shall I tell you? Speak the truth, O wide-and-red-eyed one.
Thus ends the one hundred and seventh chapter, entitled 'The Origin of the Planets, Lunar Mansions, and so forth,' in the first book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara, in the conversation between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.

1.108.s:
.. vajra uvāca .. ..
dakṣasya vaṃśaṃ sakalaṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ ca saṃbhavam ..
tvatto'haṃ śrotumicchāmi sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ vara .. 1 ..
1.108.d:
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥ ॥
दक्षस्य वंशं सकलं नक्षत्राणां च संभवम् ॥
त्वत्तोऽहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि सर्वधर्मभृतां वर ॥ 1 ॥
1.108.m:
Vajra said:
I wish to hear from you the entire lineage of Dakṣa
And the origin of the lunar mansions, O best of all maintainers of dharma.

1.108.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
auttānapādirdharmātmā dhruvaḥ pūrvaṃ mayoditaḥ ..
dhruvastvajanayatsṛṣṭiṃ mahābalapagakramām .. 2 ..
1.108.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
औत्तानपादिर्धर्मात्मा ध्रुवः पूर्वं मयोदितः ॥
ध्रुवस्त्वजनयत्सृष्टिं महाबलपगक्रमाम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.108.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Dhruva, the son of Uttānapāda, devoted to dharma, was previously spoken of by me.
Dhruva indeed begot offspring of great strength and prowess.

1.108.s:
tasya prācīnagarbhastu putrastasyāpyudāradhīḥ ..
divaṃjayastasya sutastasya putro ripuḥ smṛtaḥ .. 3 ..
1.108.d:
तस्य प्राचीनगर्भस्तु पुत्रस्तस्याप्युदारधीः ॥
दिवंजयस्तस्य सुतस्तस्य पुत्रो रिपुः स्मृतः ॥ 3 ॥
1.108.m:
His son was Prācīnagarbha; and his [son] of noble intellect
Was Divaṃjaya; his son is remembered as Ripu.

1.108.s:
ripoḥ putrastathā śrīmāṃścākṣuṣaḥ kīrtito manuḥ ..
ūrustasya sutaḥ śrīmānaṅgastasyāpyathātmajaḥ .. 4 ..
1.108.d:
रिपोः पुत्रस्तथा श्रीमांश्चाक्षुषः कीर्तितो मनुः ॥
ऊरुस्तस्य सुतः श्रीमानङ्गस्तस्याप्यथात्मजः ॥ 4 ॥
1.108.m:
The son of Ripu is proclaimed as the glorious Cākṣuṣa Manu;
His son was the glorious Ūru, and his son then was Aṅga.

1.108.s:
atrirjagrāha taṃ putraṃ dattakaṃ tu yaśasvine ..
aṅgasya venaḥ putrastu nāstiko dharmavarjitaḥ .. 5 ..
1.108.d:
अत्रिर्जग्राह तं पुत्रं दत्तकं तु यशस्विने ॥
अङ्गस्य वेनः पुत्रस्तु नास्तिको धर्मवर्जितः ॥ 5 ॥
1.108.m:
Atri took him as an adopted son for the renowned one.
The son of Aṅga was Vena, an atheist devoid of dharma,

1.108.s:
asacchāstrarato nityaṃ lokāyatikasattamaḥ ..
cakāra loke maryādāṃ dharmabāhyo narādhipaḥ .. 6 ..
1.108.d:
असच्छास्त्ररतो नित्यं लोकायतिकसत्तमः ॥
चकार लोके मर्यादां धर्मबाह्यो नराधिपः ॥ 6 ॥
1.108.m:
Constantly devoted to false treatises, the foremost of the Lokāyatikas.
That ruler of men, outside of dharma, established a rule in the world:

1.108.s:
na yaṣṭavyaṃ na hotavyaṃ na deyaṃ dharmakāraṇam ..
ṛṣayastaṃ samāgamya kadācidvākyamabruvan .. 7 ..
1.108.d:
न यष्टव्यं न होतव्यं न देयं धर्मकारणम् ॥
ऋषयस्तं समागम्य कदाचिद्वाक्यमब्रुवन् ॥ 7 ॥
1.108.m:
'No sacrifice is to be performed, no oblation made, no gift given for the sake of dharma.'
The sages approached him once and spoke these words:

1.108.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
pūrvapravṛttāṃ maryādāṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraiḥ kṛtām ..
lokāyatikavākyena na tvaṃ hantumihārhasi .. 8 ..
1.108.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
पूर्वप्रवृत्तां मर्यादां पूर्वैः पूर्वतरैः कृताम् ॥
लोकायतिकवाक्येन न त्वं हन्तुमिहार्हसि ॥ 8 ॥
1.108.m:
The sages said:
The ancient boundary established by ancestors and those even earlier
You should not destroy here on the word of a Lokāyatika.

1.108.s:
karmaṇā sukṛteneha sukhaṃ jantu samaśnute ..
duḥkhaṃ jantuśca prāpnoti duṣkṛtena ca karmaṇā .. 9 ..
1.108.d:
कर्मणा सुकृतेनेह सुखं जन्तु समश्नुते ॥
दुःखं जन्तुश्च प्राप्नोति दुष्कृतेन च कर्मणा ॥ 9 ॥
1.108.m:
By good action a creature enjoys happiness here,
And a creature attains sorrow by evil action.

1.108.s:
ye yajante sadā devānguruśuśrūṣakāśca ye ..
viprapūjāratā ye ca tīrthayātrāratāśca ye . 1.108.10 ..
1.108.d:
ये यजन्ते सदा देवान्गुरुशुश्रूषकाश्च ये ॥
विप्रपूजारता ये च तीर्थयात्रारताश्च ये । 1.108.10 ॥
1.108.m:
Those who always sacrifice to the gods, and those who serve their elders,
Those who are devoted to honouring brahmins, and those who are devoted to pilgrimages to sacred fords,

1.108.s:
tapasvinaḥ satyaratā ye ca dāne sadā ratāḥ ..
samaśnuvanti bhūpāla paraloke sukhāni te .. 11 ..
1.108.d:
तपस्विनः सत्यरता ये च दाने सदा रताः ॥
समश्नुवन्ति भूपाल परलोके सुखानि ते ॥ 11 ॥
1.108.m:
Those of ascetic practice, devoted to truth, and those who are always devoted to giving—
They enjoy pleasures in the next world, O protector of the earth.

1.108.s:
sa tvaṃ sukhaparibhraṣṭānnṛlokāngantumarhasi ..
vena uvāca ..
bhavatāṃ kiṃ pralāpena vṛthaiva dvijapuṅgavāḥ .. 12 ..
1.108.d:
स त्वं सुखपरिभ्रष्टान्नृलोकान्गन्तुमर्हसि ॥
वेन उवाच ॥
भवतां किं प्रलापेन वृथैव द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥ 12 ॥
1.108.m:
You ought not to go to human worlds that have fallen from happiness.
Vena said:
What is the use of your prattle, in vain indeed, O bulls among the twice-born?

1.108.s:
ye mṛtāste mṛtāḥ sarve mṛtānāṃ sambhavaḥ kutaḥ ..
prāṇasya vāyubhūtasya niṣkrāntasya śarīrataḥ .. 13 ..
1.108.d:
ये मृतास्ते मृताः सर्वे मृतानां सम्भवः कुतः ॥
प्राणस्य वायुभूतस्य निष्क्रान्तस्य शरीरतः ॥ 13 ॥
1.108.m:
Those who have died are all dead; whence could there be rebirth for the dead,
when the breath of life, turned to wind, has departed from the body?

1.108.s:
bhūyaḥ śarīragrahaṇaṃ yuktyā naivopapadyate ..
tapāṃsi hāyanāścitrāḥ saṃyamo bhogavañcanā .. 14 ..
1.108.d:
भूयः शरीरग्रहणं युक्त्या नैवोपपद्यते ॥
तपांसि हायनाश्चित्राः संयमो भोगवञ्चना ॥ 14 ॥
1.108.m:
Taking up a body once again cannot be established through reason at all.
Austerities over diverse years, self-restraint—these are merely deprivation of pleasure.

1.108.s:
agnihotrādikaṃ karma bālakrīḍeva lakṣyate ..
grāmyāṇāṃ mūḍhacittānāṃ sragviṇāṃ caiva yoṣitām .. 15 ..
1.108.d:
अग्निहोत्रादिकं कर्म बालक्रीडेव लक्ष्यते ॥
ग्राम्याणां मूढचित्तानां स्रग्विणां चैव योषिताम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.108.m:
Rituals such as the Agnihotra appear just like child's play.
In order to take the wealth of rustic, foolish-minded folk,

1.108.s:
anyeṣāṃ caiva dhanināṃ dhūrterādi tsubhirdhanam ..
śāstrāṇyanekarūpāṇi grathitāni sahasraśaḥ .. 16 ..
1.108.d:
अन्येषां चैव धनिनां धूर्तेरादि त्सुभिर्धनम् ॥
शास्त्राण्यनेकरूपाणि ग्रथितानि सहस्रशः ॥ 16 ॥
1.108.m:
and of garlanded women, and of other wealthy men,
rogues have composed multifaceted scriptures by the thousands:

1.108.s:
dehi nityaṃ yajasvaivaṃ devāste'nugrahīkṛtāḥ ..
dhanamāpsyasi śatrūṃśca vijeṣyasi sukhaṃ ca te .. 17 ..
1.108.d:
देहि नित्यं यजस्वैवं देवास्तेऽनुग्रहीकृताः ॥
धनमाप्स्यसि शत्रूंश्च विजेष्यसि सुखं च ते ॥ 17 ॥
1.108.m:
"Give constantly! Sacrifice thus! The gods will be gracious to you!
You will obtain wealth, conquer your enemies, and have happiness!"

1.108.s:
mugdhā evaṃ pratāryante dhūrtairdhanajihīrṣayā ..
yāvajjīvaṃ sukhaṃ jīvennāsti mṛtyoragocaram .. 18 ..
1.108.d:
मुग्धा एवं प्रतार्यन्ते धूर्तैर्धनजिहीर्षया ॥
यावज्जीवं सुखं जीवेन्नास्ति मृत्योरगोचरम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.108.m:
In this way the naive are deceived by rogues eager to seize their wealth.
As long as one lives, one should live happily; nothing is beyond the reach of death.

1.108.s:
bhasmībhūtasya śāntasya punarāgamanaṃ kutaḥ ..
nāsti dattaṃ hutaṃ ceṣṭaṃ na devā ṛṣayo na ca .. 19 ..
1.108.d:
भस्मीभूतस्य शान्तस्य पुनरागमनं कुतः ॥
नास्ति दत्तं हुतं चेष्टं न देवा ऋषयो न च ॥ 19 ॥
1.108.m:
When one has been reduced to ashes and extinguished, whence comes any return?
There is no gift, no offering, no sacrifice, nor are there gods, nor seers.

1.108.s:
mayāptaṃ bhuvi rājyaṃ ca bhogāścānye pṛthagvidhāḥ..
kathaṃ prāptaṃ hi tyakṣyāmi bhavatāṃ vacanena vai .. 1.108.20 ..
1.108.d:
मयाप्तं भुवि राज्यं च भोगाश्चान्ये पृथग्विधाः॥
कथं प्राप्तं हि त्यक्ष्यामि भवतां वचनेन वै ॥ 1.108.20 ॥
1.108.m:
Sovereignty on earth has been gained by me, as well as various other enjoyments.
How indeed shall I abandon what has been attained, merely at your word?

1.108.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
etacchrutvā vacastasya venasya nṛpasattama ..
ṛṣayastamathocuste rājānaṃ duṣṭacetasam .. 21..
1.108.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य वेनस्य नृपसत्तम ॥
ऋषयस्तमथोचुस्ते राजानं दुष्टचेतसम् ॥ 21॥
1.108.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having heard these words of Vena, O best of kings,
the seers then addressed that evil-minded ruler.

1.108.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
naitadaupayikaṃ vākyaṃ dhruvavaṃśodbhavasya te ..
pratyakṣaṃ karmaṇāṃ loke phalaṃ pārthiva dṛśyate .. 22..
1.108.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
नैतदौपयिकं वाक्यं ध्रुववंशोद्भवस्य ते ॥
प्रत्यक्षं कर्मणां लोके फलं पार्थिव दृश्यते ॥ 22॥
1.108.m:
The seers said:
This speech is not befitting for you who are born of Dhruva's lineage.
The visible fruit of actions, O king, is seen in the world.

1.108.s:
kāṅkṣyamāṇāñjanānpaśya bhojanācchādanaṃ param ..
sahasraṃbharakānanyānpaśya bhūpāla mānavān ..23..
1.108.d:
काङ्क्ष्यमाणाञ्जनान्पश्य भोजनाच्छादनं परम् ॥
सहस्रंभरकानन्यान्पश्य भूपाल मानवान् ॥23॥
1.108.m:
Behold the people begging for nothing more than food and clothing!
Behold other men, O king, supporting thousands,

1.108.s:
śibikābhyastathaivānyāngacchamānānyathāsukham ..
kṣudhayā ca parītāṃśca śākocchiṣṭabhujastathā .. 24 ..
1.108.d:
शिबिकाभ्यस्तथैवान्यान्गच्छमानान्यथासुखम् ॥
क्षुधया च परीतांश्च शाकोच्छिष्टभुजस्तथा ॥ 24 ॥
1.108.m:
and others traveling comfortably in palanquins as they please,
and also those gripped by hunger, eating vegetable scraps,

1.108.s:
kāṣṭhabhārasamākrāntānparibhūtānparaistathā ..
jugupsitām̐stathā dīnānbahuśalyānnarām̐stathā .. 28 ..
1.108.d:
काष्ठभारसमाक्रान्तान्परिभूतान्परैस्तथा ॥
जुगुप्सिताम्̐स्तथा दीनान्बहुशल्यान्नराम्̐स्तथा ॥ 28 ॥
1.108.m:
overburdened with loads of firewood, humiliated by others,
and likewise men who are despised, wretched, and pierced by many thorns,

1.108.s:
paṅgūnanyānkubjakāṃśca kuṣṭhajvaravipīḍitān ..
raugairbahubhirākrāntānparibhūtānparaistathā..26..
1.108.d:
पङ्गूनन्यान्कुब्जकांश्च कुष्ठज्वरविपीडितान् ॥
रौगैर्बहुभिराक्रान्तान्परिभूतान्परैस्तथा॥26॥
1.108.m:
others who are lame and hunchbacked, afflicted with leprosy and fever,
overwhelmed by numerous diseases, and despised by others,

1.108.s:
tārkikānkṛpaṇāndīnānvyādhigrastānsukhacyutān..
iṣṭabandhuviyogārtānpaśya pāpena mānavān ..27..
1.108.d:
तार्किकान्कृपणान्दीनान्व्याधिग्रस्तान्सुखच्युतान्॥
इष्टबन्धुवियोगार्तान्पश्य पापेन मानवान् ॥27॥
1.108.m:
disputatious, miserable, wretched, seized by illness, fallen from happiness,
afflicted by separation from beloved kin—behold these men [suffering] through sin!

1.108.s:
ārogyarūpasattvaujodhanadhānyasamanvitān ..
dharmeṇa ca janānpaśya bandhubhṛtyasamanvitān..28..
1.108.d:
आरोग्यरूपसत्त्वौजोधनधान्यसमन्वितान् ॥
धर्मेण च जनान्पश्य बन्धुभृत्यसमन्वितान्॥28॥
1.108.m:
And behold people endowed with health, beauty, vitality, vigor, wealth, and grain,
endowed with kin and servants, [reaping] through dharma!

1.108.s:
rājamārgamimaṃ lokāstava karmānuvartate ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
tatasteṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā ṛṣīṇāmugracetasām .. 29 ..
1.108.d:
राजमार्गमिमं लोकास्तव कर्मानुवर्तते ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
ततस्तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा ऋषीणामुग्रचेतसाम् ॥ 29 ॥
1.108.m:
This royal highway of action follows your subjects.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Then, having heard that speech of the fierce-minded seers,

1.108.s:
hastena hastaṃ saṃghaṭya prahasam̐stānuvāca ha ..
vena uvāca ..
śubhena karmaṇā saukhyaṃ duḥkhaṃ pāpena karmaṇā .. 1.108.30 ..
1.108.d:
हस्तेन हस्तं संघट्य प्रहसम्̐स्तानुवाच ह ॥
वेन उवाच ॥
शुभेन कर्मणा सौख्यं दुःखं पापेन कर्मणा ॥ 1.108.30 ॥
1.108.m:
clapping hand against hand and laughing aloud, he spoke to them.
Vena said:
People do not obtain happiness through good action,

1.108.s:
nāpnuvanti janā viprāḥ prāpnuvanti svabhāvataḥ ..
svabhāvaśca vicitro'yaṃ saṃsārodvejakaḥ sadā .. 31 ..
1.108.d:
नाप्नुवन्ति जना विप्राः प्राप्नुवन्ति स्वभावतः ॥
स्वभावश्च विचित्रोऽयं संसारोद्वेजकः सदा ॥ 31 ॥
1.108.m:
nor misery through sinful action, O brahmins; they obtain them through nature.
And this nature is varied, constantly agitating the worldly realm.

1.108.s:
nātra pūrvakṛtaṃ karma dhūrtavādo yathā dvijāḥ ..
aśmānaḥ karmaṇā kena sūkṣmāścānye mahattarāḥ .. 32 ..
1.108.d:
नात्र पूर्वकृतं कर्म धूर्तवादो यथा द्विजाः ॥
अश्मानः कर्मणा केन सूक्ष्माश्चान्ये महत्तराः ॥ 32 ॥
1.108.m:
Here there is no past action; that is the talk of rogues, O twice-born!
By what action are stones fine, and others huge?

1.108.s:
vinyastāḥ karmaṇā kena surārcāpāpabhūmiṣu ..
pāṣāṇārcādidattena kathaṃ tuṣyanti devatāḥ .. 33 ..
1.108.d:
विन्यस्ताः कर्मणा केन सुरार्चापापभूमिषु ॥
पाषाणार्चादिदत्तेन कथं तुष्यन्ति देवताः ॥ 33 ॥
1.108.m:
By what action are they placed as divine icons, or onto defiled grounds?
How can deities be pleased by what is offered to a stone icon or the like?

1.108.s:
ke deśā na mayā dṛṣṭā nāpi pūrvaṃ pitāmahaḥ ..
nānyairjanyaistathā tāṃśca dhūrtavākyātpratīmahe .. 34 ..
1.108.d:
के देशा न मया दृष्टा नापि पूर्वं पितामहः ॥
नान्यैर्जन्यैस्तथा तांश्च धूर्तवाक्यात्प्रतीमहे ॥ 34 ॥
1.108.m:
Which regions were not seen by me, nor previously by my grandfather?
Nor [were they seen] by other people; and yet we are to believe them on the word of rogues!

1.108.s:
anyabhuktena cānyasya tṛptiścaiva kathaṃ bhavet ..
anyabhuktena cānyasya yadi tṛptirbhavi ṣyati .. 35 ..
1.108.d:
अन्यभुक्तेन चान्यस्य तृप्तिश्चैव कथं भवेत् ॥
अन्यभुक्तेन चान्यस्य यदि तृप्तिर्भवि ष्यति ॥ 35 ॥
1.108.m:
And how could satisfaction arise for one through food eaten by another?
If one were to find satisfaction through what is eaten by another,

1.108.s:
dadyātpravasite śrāddhaṃ na sa pathyaudanaṃ mahat ..
mṛtasya pakṣe dagdhasya bhasmībhūtasya vā punaḥ .. 36 ..
1.108.d:
दद्यात्प्रवसिते श्राद्धं न स पथ्यौदनं महत् ॥
मृतस्य पक्षे दग्धस्य भस्मीभूतस्य वा पुनः ॥ 36 ॥
1.108.m:
then one might perform a śrāddha for a traveler, without giving him a substantial meal for his journey!
In the case of a dead man who has been burnt, or rather, reduced to ashes,

1.108.s:
sarvabhāvavinaṣṭasya kiṃ nu śrāddhaiḥ prayojanam ..
kṛpaṇairyaja dehīti dhanalubdhaiḥ prakīrtitam .. 37 ..
1.108.d:
सर्वभावविनष्टस्य किं नु श्राद्धैः प्रयोजनम् ॥
कृपणैर्यज देहीति धनलुब्धैः प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 37 ॥
1.108.m:
and whose entire being is destroyed, of what use could śrāddha rituals be?
"Sacrifice! Give!"—this has been proclaimed by wretched men greedy for wealth,

1.108.s:
dhanināṃ dhananāśāya satataṃ svārthatatparaiḥ ..
dharme niviṣṭāḥ puruṣā dṛśyante duḥkhajīvinaḥ .. 38 ..
1.108.d:
धनिनां धननाशाय सततं स्वार्थतत्परैः ॥
धर्मे निविष्टाः पुरुषा दृश्यन्ते दुःखजीविनः ॥ 38 ॥
1.108.m:
intent ever on self-interest, for the destruction of the wealth of the rich.
Men devoted to dharma are seen living in sorrow,

1.108.s:
sukhānvitā hi dṛśyante pāpakarmaratāstathā ..
tasmāddharmeṇa kiṃ kāryaṃ sukhaṃ jīvettu paṇḍitaḥ ..
puruṣārthaḥ paraḥ kāmo dhanena ca tadāpyate ..39..
1.108.d:
सुखान्विता हि दृश्यन्ते पापकर्मरतास्तथा ॥
तस्माद्धर्मेण किं कार्यं सुखं जीवेत्तु पण्डितः ॥
पुरुषार्थः परः कामो धनेन च तदाप्यते ॥39॥
1.108.m:
while those devoted to sinful acts are seen filled with happiness.
Therefore, what is the use of dharma? A wise man should live happily!
Pleasure is the supreme aim of human life, and it is attained through wealth.

1.108.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
pratyakṣameva paśyantaḥ pūrvajanmani mānavāḥ ..1.108.40..
1.108.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
प्रत्यक्षमेव पश्यन्तः पूर्वजन्मनि मानवाः ॥1.108.40॥
1.108.m:
The seers said:
Beholding only the immediate present, men in their previous birth,

1.108.s:
paralokaṃ na paśyanti paśya devena vañcitāḥ ..
jātamātro yathā jantustanaṃ gṛhṇāti pārthiva .. 41 ..
1.108.d:
परलोकं न पश्यन्ति पश्य देवेन वञ्चिताः ॥
जातमात्रो यथा जन्तुस्तनं गृह्णाति पार्थिव ॥ 41 ॥
1.108.m:
deceived by fate, do not see the other world, look!
Just as a newborn creature grasps the breast, O king—

1.108.s:
pūrvajanmāntarābhyāsaṃ vinā tatkasya ceṣṭitam ..
prāṇena vāyubhūtena janmanyasminyathā naraḥ .. 42 ..
1.108.d:
पूर्वजन्मान्तराभ्यासं विना तत्कस्य चेष्टितम् ॥
प्राणेन वायुभूतेन जन्मन्यस्मिन्यथा नरः ॥ 42 ॥
1.108.m:
without practice in another previous birth, whose doing could that be?
Just as in this birth a man assumes a body

1.108.s:
karoti dehagrahaṇaṃ janmāntaragatastathā ..
mahīvikāramaśmānaḥ karmajīvavivarjitān .. 43 ..
1.108.d:
करोति देहग्रहणं जन्मान्तरगतस्तथा ॥
महीविकारमश्मानः कर्मजीवविवर्जितान् ॥ 43 ॥
1.108.m:
by means of the breath turned to wind, so does he when gone to another birth.
Stones are modifications of the earth, devoid of action and soul;

1.108.s:
sūkṣmatvaṃ ca mahattvaṃ ca teṣāmīśvarakāritam ..
mantreṇa nīyate śrāddhaṃ paralokagate jane .. 44 ..
1.108.d:
सूक्ष्मत्वं च महत्त्वं च तेषामीश्वरकारितम् ॥
मन्त्रेण नीयते श्राद्धं परलोकगते जने ॥ 44 ॥
1.108.m:
both their smallness and their greatness are brought about by the Lord.
The śrāddha offering is conveyed through mantra when a person has gone to the next world;

1.108.s:
dṛṣṭaḥ pravāsino naiva tathā mantrasya pārthiva ..
prākāmyayuktā devāśca yuktā laghimanā tathā .. 45 ..
1.108.d:
दृष्टः प्रवासिनो नैव तथा मन्त्रस्य पार्थिव ॥
प्राकाम्ययुक्ता देवाश्च युक्ता लघिमना तथा ॥ 45 ॥
1.108.m:
no such mantra is seen for a traveler, O king.
The gods are endowed with irresistible will and endowed with lightness;

1.108.s:
jñānayuktāśca gṛhṇanti sarvatra viniveditam ..
dharmamāsevatāṃ nṛṇāṃ vipattiryā narādhipa .. 46 ..
1.108.d:
ज्ञानयुक्ताश्च गृह्णन्ति सर्वत्र विनिवेदितम् ॥
धर्ममासेवतां नृणां विपत्तिर्या नराधिप ॥ 46 ॥
1.108.m:
endowed with knowledge, they receive what is offered anywhere.
The adversity, O ruler of men, that befalls men practicing dharma,

1.108.s:
pūrvajanmakṛteneha sukṛtena ca karmaṇā ..
